name: Flame Chompers
summary: 'Play me' always lands at base; no option to play to a battlefield you control.
detail: playIgnoringCost(ctx.controller, ctx.source) is called with no location, so it defaults to base. A played unit may go to base or a battlefield you control (CR 355.2.a).

name: Magma Wurm
summary: 'Other friendly units enter ready' is not implemented (stub with ENGINE GAP comment).
detail: The class has only def(). resolvePermanent only consults the entering card's own entersReadyOnPlay() and The Exile, so other friendly units still enter exhausted while Magma Wurm is in play.

name: Captain Farron
summary: Farron himself is given printed Assault 1 (assault_value=1 + Keyword::Assault), but the text grants Assault only to OTHER friendly units.
detail: def sets d.assault_value = 1 and keywords.set(Keyword::Assault). recomputeMight adds assault_value while attacking, so Farron gets +1 [M] as an attacker that the card does not have. The aura itself correctly excludes Farron.

name: Dangerous Duo
summary: The Legion +2 [M] never applies: triggered abilities go on the chain with no targets, and onTrigger only acts on targets[0].
detail: TriggerManager::fireTrigger calls chain_.addAbility(source, controller, def) with empty targets. chooseTargetsAtFinalize returns early for non-activated abilities unless kFinalizeTrigger is set. Nothing fills item.targets for a WhenYouPlayMe trigger, so 'give a unit +2 [M]' is a silent no-op. It should use pickTarget (choicesAtFinalization). First Mate, Gem Jammer and Aspiring Engineer use the same pattern.

name: Noxus Saboteur
summary: 'Your opponents' [Hidden] cards can't be revealed here' is inert: the opp_hidden_unrevealable flag is set but never read.
detail: grep shows only the aura sets the flag and the engine resets it. The hidden-play generator (game_engine.cpp ~3140) never checks it, so opponents can still play their Hidden cards at Saboteur's battlefield. Playing them is how Hidden cards are revealed.

name: Sun Disc
summary: When armed, the next unit play lets the player ready ANY exhausted friendly unit on board, not the unit just played.
detail: The text says the next unit you play this turn enters ready. onTrigger builds 'legal' from every exhausted friendly unit with a location and lets pickTarget choose any of them. That turns the effect into 'ready any exhausted unit'. The played unit should be identified (e.g. via a subject), or readied as it enters.

name: Unlicensed Armory
summary: The optional '[R]' payment at death time is not modeled; the recall is automatic and free.
detail: Official text: 'you may pay [R] to recall it exhausted instead'. Code sets death_replacement_recall_pending, which the engine consumes unconditionally (no confirm, no power payment), so the replacement always happens for free.
errata_note: Errata: the optional payment is [C] (Calm), not [R]; heal+exhaust+recall is correct.

name: Unlicensed Armory
summary: engine_text says pay [C] and 'heal it, exhaust it, and recall it'; official text is pay [R] to 'recall it exhausted' (no heal).
detail: The ability_text was taken from an older/incorrect wording. The engine flag also heals the unit, which the official text does not say.
errata_note: Errata 2025-10-21: engine text (pay [C], heal, exhaust, recall) is the current text.

name: Blind Fury
summary: A revealed spell is banished but never played.
detail: Text: banish it, then play it ignoring cost. Code only calls playIgnoringCost for units/gear and leaves spells banished, citing a primitive limitation that no longer exists: EffectExecutor::playIgnoringCost now queues spells on the chain (queue_spell_). Units are also always placed at base without a location choice.

name: Shakedown
summary: Opponent's option to have you draw 2 instead of taking 6 is never offered; always deals 6.
detail: Text: 'Deal 6 to it unless its controller has you draw 2.' Code unconditionally deals 6 and logs the opt-out as unmodeled. Outcome-changing for the opponent (they can never save the unit).

name: Vi, Destructive
summary: The recycle-1 cost always takes the oldest trash card and is paid at resolution instead of at activation.
detail: Players choose which card to recycle as the cost. Paying in onActivate also means the cost isn't paid up front if the ability is countered.

name: Charm
summary: 'Move an enemy unit' always moves it to base; destination is not chosen.
detail: A unit at base could legally be moved to a battlefield, and the caster cannot choose; when the target is already at base the spell does nothing.

name: Clockwork Keeper
summary: Engine text models the draw as a 'When you play me' trigger. The official text is 'As you play me, you may pay [G]... If you do, draw 1.'
detail: Here the draw is a separate trigger that can be responded to, not part of playing the card. The cost domain (Calm power) matches. The effect is nearly the same.
errata_note: Errata 2025-10-21: 'When you play me, if you paid the additional cost, draw 1' is a separate trigger.

name: Defy
summary: Only the Energy cap ([4]) is checked; the Power cap ('no more than [A]', i.e. power cost <= 1) is ignored.
detail: Resolve-time gate reads only cardDB energy_cost; a spell costing <=4 Energy with 2+ Power (e.g. Wind Wall 3+2) is wrongly counterable. Also hasLegalTargets accepts any spell and only the chain top is examined, so an ineligible top spell makes Defy fizzle even if an eligible spell is below it.

name: Meditation
summary: Optional additional cost (exhaust a friendly unit) is decided and paid at resolution, and the exhausted unit is auto-picked.
detail: Text makes it an additional cost to play, paid on cast; the code asks at resolve time and exhausts the first ready friendly unit in map order instead of letting the player choose which unit.

name: Solari Shieldbearer
summary: Stun trigger depends on targets[0], which is always empty for triggered abilities, so nothing is stunned.
detail: Same root cause as Riptide Rex: getTargetRequirements() is not used for triggered abilities. Verified with an engine probe: the enemy unit is not stunned after Shieldbearer is played.

name: Stand United
summary: 'Buffs give an additional +1 [M] to friendly units this turn' is not implemented.
detail: Only buffUnit(target) runs; the comment marks the buff-amplification rider as an ENGINE GAP. No such field exists in core/ or EffectExecutor.

name: Adaptatron
summary: 'Buff me' calls buffUnit, which always increments, so repeated conquers stack +1 buffs past the one-buff limit.
detail: CR 427.1.b.1: a unit that already has a buff counter gets no new one. EffectExecutor::buffUnit doesn't check buff_count, unlike the manual guards in Cithria, Kinkou Monk and Wildclaw Shaman. Poro Herder uses the same path, but there the unit is fresh so it rarely matters.

name: Spirit's Refuge
summary: The gear itself is given [Deflect] (keywords.set(Deflect), deflect_value=1).
detail: Only friendly buffed units should have Deflect. Setting the keyword on the gear's CardDef makes opponents pay [A] to choose Spirit's Refuge itself with a spell or ability.

name: Wizened Elder
summary: The +1 [M] while buffed is applied twice (card applyPassiveAura plus the engine's generic 'while i'm buffed ... additional +1 [m]' parser), so it gets +2.
detail: recalculateAuras step 3b (game_engine.cpp ~4740) already grants +1 from the ability_text, and the card's applyPassiveAura adds another. Probe: after cleanup with buff_count=1, aura_might_bonus=2 from 2 aura effects. The unit test calls applyPassiveAura directly, so it misses this. Also, with several Elders each instance's call loops over all instances and stacks more.

name: Blitzcrank, Impassive
summary: 'Move an enemy unit to here' always moves the first enemy unit in map order. The player gets no choice, and targeting protection is ignored.
detail: find_enemy_elsewhere() returns the first match. The player only answers yes/no. Can't-be-chosen and Deflect units aren't excluded either. It should use pickTarget over enemy units not already here, picked at finalization.

name: Solari Shrine
summary: Fires on any enemy unit death; neither 'you kill' nor 'stunned' is checked.
detail: Text: 'When you kill a stunned enemy unit'. triggerType is WhenAnEnemyUnitDies with no triggerCondition; comments admit the stunned check is skipped, and the kill-by-you requirement is also absent, so combat deaths or self-kills of unstunned enemies give a draw.

name: Taric, Protector
summary: Granted [Shield] sets only the keyword flag and never adds +1 [M] while defending.
detail: The AuraEffect has keyword=Shield but might_bonus=0. recomputeMight only adds the printed shield_value, and the aura fold only sums might_bonus. Probe: a 2-might friendly defender next to Taric has the Shield keyword but stays at 2 might. Use the auraKeyword() helper, which sets the conditional might. The engine's generic 'other friendly units here have' parser has the same gap.

name: Yasuo, Remorseful
summary: WhenIAttack damage reads targets[0], but combat triggers are fired with empty targets, so no damage is dealt.
detail: onCombatStarted -> fireTrigger -> addAbility with no targets. Also, the requirement is must_be_at_battlefield, not 'here' (same battlefield). A pickTarget restricted to enemy units at Yasuo's battlefield is needed, as Ahri, Inquisitive does.

name: Zhonya's Hourglass
summary: The replacement works while Zhonya is facedown ([Hidden]), since applyReplacement never checks is_hidden.
detail: Both replacement loops (EffectExecutor::killObject, GameEngine::killUnit) take any controller-owned object with a location, including a facedown Hidden card. A facedown card has no abilities until it is revealed/played, so Zhonya should not protect units while hidden.

name: Zhonya's Hourglass
summary: Official text is 'Recall that unit exhausted'; code (and engine_text) also heals it.
detail: Gallery: 'The next time a friendly unit would die, kill this instead. Recall that unit exhausted.' Code calls healObject before exhaust+recall. The heal matters if lethal damage can still kill the unit at base.
errata_note: Errata 2025-10-21: current text heals, exhausts and recalls.

name: Mystic Reversal
summary: 'You may make new choices for it' is not implemented; stolen spell keeps original targets.
detail: Only controller is changed on the chain-top item and object; targets/modes are retained (documented gap). Stealing e.g. a removal spell aimed at your own unit still hits your unit, which largely defeats the card. Also only the chain-top spell can be taken.

name: Whiteflame Protector
summary: +8 [M] trigger reads targets[0], which is always empty, so no unit gets the bonus.
detail: Triggered abilities get no targets from getTargetRequirements. Verified with an engine probe: neither the friendly unit nor Whiteflame got temp might.

name: Eager Apprentice
summary: The cost reduction applies to every friendly card, not only spells.
detail: The text reduces only spells' Energy cost. The code pushes an unfiltered CostModifier, as the code's own NOTE admits, so units and gear also get [1] off. Also, each on-board instance's applyPassiveAura scans for the first instance at a battlefield, so a second Apprentice sitting at base still adds a reduction.

name: Riptide Rex
summary: Play trigger reads targets[0], but triggered abilities are always added to the chain with empty targets, so the 6 damage never happens.
detail: TriggerManager::fireTrigger calls chain_.addAbility(source, controller, def) with no targets, and chooseTargetsAtFinalize only runs runFinalizePass for triggers (getTargetRequirements is ignored for triggered abilities). Verified with a scratch engine probe: playing Rex with an enemy unit at a battlefield leaves it at 0 damage. Fix: choicesAtFinalization()=kFinalizeTrigger + pickTarget, like Carnivorous Snapvine.

name: Blastcone Fae
summary: -2 [M] play trigger reads targets[0], which is always empty, so it is a no-op.
detail: Same pattern as Riptide Rex, Solari Shieldbearer and Whiteflame Protector (verified by probe): getTargetRequirements is ignored for triggers. It needs pickTarget at finalization.

name: Garbage Grabber
summary: Which 3 trash cards are recycled is picked automatically (the first three in trash), not by the player.
detail: The recycle-3 cost is also paid at resolution inside onActivate instead of at activation.

name: Gemcraft Seer
summary: 'Other friendly units have [Vision]' never takes effect: the play-time Vision peek reads obj.keywords, not aura keywords.
detail: TriggerManager::onCardPlayed (trigger_manager.cpp:317) checks obj.keywords.has(Vision). The aura is only granted at cleanup through aura_keywords, so friendly units played while the Seer is out never get the Vision look. The code comment admits this gap.

name: Portal Rescue
summary: Engine text/code have the unit's owner play it; official text says 'play it to base' (you, the caster).
detail: def text: 'its owner plays it to their base'; gallery: 'then play it to base'. Code calls playIgnoringCost(owner, ...). Differs only when you control a unit you don't own (stolen units return to the opponent).
errata_note: Errata 2025-10-21: 'its owner plays it to their base'.

name: Sprite Mother
summary: CardDef sets Keyword::Temporary on Sprite Mother herself, so she is killed at the start of her controller's next Beginning Phase.
detail: The printed text gives [Temporary] only to the Sprite token. The engine copies def.keywords onto the object, and GameEngine (~line 761) kills every unit with keywords.has(Temporary). Probe confirmed the played Sprite Mother has Temporary. Remove d.keywords.set(Keyword::Temporary).

name: Ava Achiever
summary: The CardDef gives Ava Achiever the [Hidden] keyword, which neither the engine text nor the gallery text has.
detail: d.keywords.set(Keyword::Hidden) lets Ava be hidden for [A] and played as a Reaction later. The printed card only references [Hidden] cards in hand. Separately, the [C] is paid at resolution (after finalizingChoices) instead of at finalization per CR 383.3.

name: Dr. Mundo, Expert
summary: 'Recycle 3 from your trash' always takes the 3 oldest trash cards, with no player choice.
detail: The player should choose which cards to recycle. That changes Mundo's own Might and trash-based synergies only slightly.

name: Ekko, Recurrent
summary: Deathknell readies runes but never recycles Ekko. 'Recycle me' is skipped and Ekko stays in the trash.
detail: Text: '[Deathknell] — Recycle me to ready your runes.' The code readies every exhausted friendly rune without recycling Ekko from trash to the bottom of the Main Deck. Recycling is the cost of the effect, and it was probably meant to be optional.

name: Heimerdinger, Inventor
summary: Grants only ability index 0 of each friendly card and doesn't check that it is an [E] ability.
detail: Multi-ability cards' other [E] abilities are missing, and a non-exhaust ability at index 0 would be wrongly copied. The code comment flags this as an approximation.

name: Kai'Sa, Evolutionary
summary: The spell to replay from trash is picked automatically (most recent eligible), not by the player.
detail: The player only answers yes/no. find_spell() returns the last eligible spell in trash. The text lets the player choose any spell whose Energy cost is below their points.

name: Promising Future
summary: Engine text says each player 'banishes one'; official text says 'chooses one'.
detail: The code moves the chosen card to banishment manually (no banished_owned event, so no banish triggers fire), which keeps behavior close to the official text; the def ability_text is outdated.

name: Teemo, Strategist
summary: Missing the 'or I'm played from [Hidden]' trigger in the current text. Only WhenIDefend is wired.
detail: Latest text (OGN gallery and SFD-230): 'When I defend or I'm played from [Hidden], reveal the top 5 ... Deal 1 to an enemy unit here for each card with [Hidden]'. engine_text and the code still use the older defend-only wording.
errata_note: Errata 2025-10-21: current text is defend-only; the 'played from [Hidden]' clause was removed.

name: Time Warp
summary: 'Banish this' via banishObject during onResolve is overwritten by ChainManager, leaving the card in both banishment and trash.
detail: banishObject pushes the spell to owner.banishment and sets zone=Banishment, but after onResolve ChainManager::stepResolve unconditionally sets zone=Trash and pushes it to trash (only banish_on_leave_chain diverts it). Result: object listed in both banishment and trash vectors with zone Trash, so trash-recursion effects can reuse an extra-turn spell. Should set banish_on_leave_chain instead.

name: Arena Bar
summary: Targets don't require the unit to be exhausted: any friendly unit can be buffed.
detail: Text: 'Buff an exhausted friendly unit'. TargetRequirements has no exhausted filter and there is no enumerateLegalTargets override or check in onActivate, so ready units are legal targets.

name: Cannon Barrage
summary: Deals 2 to every enemy unit on the board instead of only enemy units in combat.
detail: Text: 'Deal 2 to all enemy units in combat.' The loop only filters on location.has_value(), isUnit() and controller != ctx.controller, so enemy units at base and at non-combat battlefields are also hit.

name: Confront
summary: 'Units you play this turn enter ready' is not implemented; only Draw 1 resolves.
detail: Comment documents it as an ENGINE LIMITATION. resolvePermanent now has a player-level enter-ready path (The Exile, id 956), so a per-player 'units enter ready this turn' flag is feasible.

name: Crackshot Corsair
summary: WhenIAttack 'deal 1 to an enemy unit here' reads empty targets, so it is a no-op. The requirement also isn't limited to 'here'.
detail: Same root cause as Yasuo, Remorseful: combat triggers carry no targets. When fixed, legal targets must be enemy units at Corsair's battlefield.

name: First Mate
summary: 'Ready another unit' reads empty trigger targets, so nothing is readied. Its TargetRequirements also don't exclude First Mate itself.
detail: Probe confirmed First Mate stays exhausted and no unit is readied. Once fixed with pickTarget, the legal set must exclude ctx.source ('another').

name: Pit Rookie
summary: Buffs the first friendly unit in map order instead of letting the player choose. Because buffUnit always increments, it can also stack a second buff on an already-buffed unit.
detail: 'Buff another friendly unit' is a choice. buffUnit (effect_executor.cpp:672) does buff_count += 1 unconditionally, against CR 427.1.b.1 (a unit with a buff gets no second one). It should use pickTarget and respect the buff cap.

name: Herald of Scales
summary: The [2] reduction applies to all friendly cards, not only Dragons.
detail: The text reduces 'Your Dragons' Energy costs'. The code pushes a CostModifier with no tag filter, as its NOTE admits, so every unit, spell and gear costs [2] less (min 1).

name: Spoils of War
summary: Cost reduction checks for any unit in the opponent's trash, not an enemy unit that died this turn.
detail: Text gives [2] off only if an enemy unit has died this turn. selfCostReduction returns 2 whenever any unit card sits in the opponent's trash, so after the first enemy death in a game the spell is permanently 2 cheaper. TurnState::any_unit_died_this_turn exists but is not side-specific, so an exact fix needs a per-player this-turn death tracker.

name: Unyielding Spirit
summary: 'Prevent all spell and ability damage' only applies when the caster is the target's controller or the source's controller.
detail: The card sets the flag on the caster only. dealDamage prevents damage when either the target's controller or the source's controller has the flag. Damage the opponent's spells deal to the opponent's own units is therefore not prevented, although the text says 'all'. This is a rare edge case.

name: Wallop
summary: The optional 'spend a buff to ignore this spell's cost' is not implemented.
detail: The text lets you spend a buff as an additional cost and then play the spell for free. The code says this is an engine limitation and always charges the printed cost.

name: Wildclaw Shaman
summary: The 'spend a buff' cost is never paid. Accepting buffs and readies the Shaman for free.
detail: Text: 'you may spend a buff to buff me and ready me'. The code asks yes/no and then buffs and readies without removing a buff from any friendly unit. still_legal also doesn't require a buff to exist. The cost should be paid at finalization (costDueNow), from a friendly unit the player picks.

name: Anivia, Primal
summary: Deals 3 to enemy units at every battlefield, not just 'here'.
detail: The filter is only isAtBattlefield(). It never compares the unit's battlefieldId with Anivia's battlefield, so enemy units at the other battlefield are hit too.

name: Kraken Hunter
summary: The optional buff-spend additional cost (reduce my cost by [O] per buff spent) is not implemented.
detail: The code comment documents it as an engine limitation. The card always costs full price and no buffs can be spent.

name: Overt Operation
summary: Spending a buff costs the unit 2 Might (buff_count and temp_might_bonus are both reduced), and the final buff stacks on units that already have one.
detail: recomputeMight already counts buff_count, so 'u.buff_count -= 1; u.temp_might_bonus -= 1' leaves the unit at -1 Might for the turn after it is re-buffed. 'Then buff all friendly units' calls buffUnit on every unit, and buffUnit always increments, so a unit that kept its buff ends up with 2 buffs. The text says only units without a buff get one. The spend-to-ready choice is also a single yes/no for all units rather than one per unit (simplification).

name: Udyr, Wildman
summary: Udyr has a permanent base [Ganking] keyword, but the card only grants Ganking through one of its modes.
detail: The official text has no [Ganking] keyword line; [Ganking] only shows up inside the 'Give me [Ganking] this turn' mode. def() still sets keywords.set(Keyword::Ganking), so Udyr can always move between battlefields and the fourth mode does nothing. This looks like a keyword parsed out of the mode text.

name: Udyr, Wildman
summary: The 'Spend my buff' cost is paid when the ability resolves, not when it is activated.
detail: getActivationCost() is empty; the buff is subtracted inside onActivate after the mode is picked. With one buff, the player can put several activations on the chain; the extra ones resolve with no effect, and an opponent can respond before the cost is paid. Sett, Brawler (0164 line 43) has the same pattern.

name: Volibear, Imposing
summary: Volibear never draws while he is in base, although with no battlefield every battlefield is 'other than mine'; he also triggers once per moved unit, not once per move.
detail: The code returns when Volibear is not at a battlefield. The reminder text '(Bases are not battlefield)' suggests he should still draw from base. trigger_manager fires once per moved unit, so moving several enemy units at once draws several cards. Line 28 also calls getObject(ctx.source) without checking objectExists. Both readings need a rules check.

name: Dazzling Aurora
summary: engine_text/code banish the revealed unit before playing it; official text just plays it.
detail: Gallery: 'reveal ... until you reveal a unit. Play it, ignoring its cost, and recycle the rest.' Code calls banishObject (which can fire banish triggers) before playIgnoringCost. The final result is otherwise the same.
errata_note: Errata 2025-10-21: 'until you reveal a unit and banish it'.

name: Ember Monk
summary: Ember Monk is given the [Hidden] keyword, which it does not have.
detail: The text is only 'When you play a card from [Hidden], give me +2 [M] this turn.' The card itself is not Hidden (the gallery entry confirms this). def() sets Keyword::Hidden, and game_engine.cpp:2875 then offers to hide Ember Monk facedown. This looks like a keyword parsed from the text.

name: Fight or Flight
summary: The target is any unit, but the text says 'a unit from a battlefield'.
detail: getTargetRequirements omits must_be_at_battlefield, so units already in base are legal targets and the effect does nothing to them. The spell can therefore be played with no unit at a battlefield.

name: Ride the Wind
summary: 'Move a friendly unit' always moves the unit to base.
detail: The code calls moveToBase unconditionally. A unit in base cannot be moved to a battlefield (the main use of the card), and a unit at a battlefield cannot move to another legal location. The destination should be the player's choice.

name: Pack of Wonders
summary: Facedown [Hidden] cards that aren't units or gear (e.g. hidden spells) can't be chosen.
detail: Text allows 'another friendly gear, unit, or [Hidden] card'. The legal list is filtered by isUnit()||isGear(), so a facedown hidden spell at a battlefield is never a legal choice.

name: Scrapheap
summary: The 'discarded' clause is not wired, though TriggerType::WhenIAmDiscarded now exists.
detail: triggerTypes() returns only WhenYouPlayThis and WhenIDie. The comment says no discard dispatch exists, but TriggerManager fires WhenIAmDiscarded from trash (trigger_manager.cpp:1146), so discarding Scrapheap should draw 1 and does not.

name: Treasure Trove
summary: 'Leaves the board' is modeled as WhenIDie only; bounce or banish gives no draw or channel.
detail: Self-documented as PARTIAL. Returning it to hand, banishing it, or recycling it does not fire the draw + exhausted channel.

name: Zaunite Bouncer
summary: 'Another unit' is not enforced, so Bouncer can return itself if it was played to a battlefield.
detail: TargetRequirements has no way to exclude the source, and the default target enumerator gets no source. If Bouncer enters at a battlefield (for example with the Miss Fortune, Buccaneer grant), it is a legal target for its own bounce.

name: Maddened Marauder
summary: 'Move a unit from a battlefield to its base' can target a unit that is already in a base.
detail: TargetRequirements is missing must_be_at_battlefield, so a unit in a base (including Marauder itself) can be chosen. That lets the player turn the mandatory move into a no-op, which the text does not allow when a unit is at a battlefield.

name: Nocturne, Horrifying
summary: Nocturne is played for free instead of for [A].
detail: The text says 'you may play me for [A]'. The code calls playIgnoringCost (a TODO in the code says so), so no power is paid. It could use playPayingCost with a [A] override. The two 'may' choices are also merged into one.

name: Nocturne, Horrifying
summary: The engine text ('look at or reveal, you may banish me') differs from the gallery wording ('look at cards from the top (and don't draw them) and see me').
detail: The gallery text has no banish step and is limited to looking without drawing. The code follows the engine wording: it banishes and then plays. It only fires on a CardRevealedEvent from the MainDeck, so it may miss 'look at' effects that don't emit that event. Check which wording is the current errata.
errata_note: Errata 2025-10-21: 'As you look at or reveal me ... you may banish me'.

name: Twisted Fate, Gambler
summary: When the trigger resumes after a target choice, it reveals and recycles a second rune.
detail: The trigger pops the top rune and recycles it before pickTarget is called. There is no choicesAtFinalization, so pickTarget suspends during resolution, and the resume runs onTrigger again from the top: it reads the new rune_deck.back(), reveals it, recycles it and branches on that rune's domain. The [R] and [Y] branches with any legal targets therefore cycle two runes, and can resolve the wrong domain's effect using the target chosen for the first one.

name: Possession
summary: The recall is done with moveToBase, which emits a UnitMovedEvent even though the text says 'This isn't a move'.
detail: moveToBase emits UnitMovedEvent (is_standard_move=false), so 'when a unit moves' triggers may fire on the recall. The engine's own death-replacement recall does the same, so this may be engine-wide.

name: Back to Back
summary: Only one friendly unit gets +2; the text says two friendly units each get +2.
detail: TargetRequirements count=1 and onResolve buffs only targets[0], so the second unit's +2 [M] is missing.

name: Call to Glory
summary: The optional 'spend a buff to ignore this spell's cost' is not implemented.
detail: The code's own log says the buff-spend-for-free option is unmodeled, so the spell always costs its printed amount.

name: Cruel Patron
summary: The additional cost 'kill a friendly unit' is handled as a play trigger, so Patron can be played without a friendly unit to kill.
detail: The engine has no kill-as-cost hook. Patron can be played with no other friendly unit (the trigger just does nothing), and the kill happens later at trigger resolution instead of as part of playing the card. The result changes: a 4-cost 6-might unit becomes available with no sacrifice.

name: Cull the Weak
summary: The opponent's unit to kill is the first one found in object-map order, not the opponent's choice.
detail: Each player should choose which of their own units dies. The opponent's pick is hard-coded to the first unit iterated, which can be their best unit. A requestChoice to the opponent (as Acceptable Losses does) is possible. This changes outcomes.

name: Forge of the Future
summary: Both clauses are wrong or missing: the play trigger kills targets[0] instead of making a Recruit token, and 'Kill this: Recycle up to 4' is absent.
detail: onTrigger(WhenYouPlayThis) calls killObject(targets[0]). With no target requirements it is a no-op; if targets were ever supplied it would kill something. No 1 [M] Recruit token is created and there is no activated ability for 'Kill this: Recycle up to 4 cards from trashes'.

name: Imperial Decree
summary: Kills units that are already damaged instead of making damage taken this turn lethal.
detail: The text creates a this-turn effect: when any unit takes damage, kill it. The code instead immediately kills every unit with damage_marked>0, which the text never does, and it ignores all damage dealt later in the turn.

name: Spectral Matron
summary: 'No more than [A]' is read as 'energy cost at most the player's available power' instead of 'Power cost at most 1'.
detail: The text limits the unit to energy cost <= 3 and Power cost <= [A] (one power of any domain). The code ignores the unit's power_cost and compares its energy_cost to the number of ready runes plus floating power. As a result it allows units with Power cost 2 or more, and blocks valid units when few runes are ready.

name: Albus Ferros
summary: The player picks how many buffs to spend, but not which units lose them (the code takes them in map order).
detail: The text lets the player spend any buffs they choose. The code removes buffs from friendly units in iteration order, so which units lose their +1 [M] is not a player decision.

name: Commander Ledros
summary: The optional cost reduction (kill friendly units, pay [Y] less per kill) is not implemented.
detail: The file has an ENGINE GAP comment; there is no additional-cost hook and no selfCostReduction. Ledros always costs the full 6 energy and 4 power, which makes him close to unplayable compared with the real card.

name: Fiora, Victorious
summary: Deflect, Ganking and Shield are set as base keywords, so Fiora has them even when she is not Mighty.
detail: The text says 'While I'm [Mighty], I have [Deflect], [Ganking], and [Shield].' applyPassiveAura grants them correctly through auras when might >= 5, but def() also sets all three keywords plus shield_value and deflect_value. hasKeyword checks base keywords, so a 4-might Fiora always has them and the condition does nothing.

name: Grand Strategem
summary: Gives +5 to one targeted friendly unit instead of all friendly units.
detail: The text says 'Give friendly units +5 [M] this turn' with no target. The code uses one friendly target and buffs only that unit.

name: Karma, Channeler
summary: Buffing a unit that already has a buff adds a second buff.
detail: A buff is only given if the unit doesn't already have one. EffectExecutor::buffUnit always does buff_count += 1, and Karma calls it with no check, so repeated recycles keep adding +1 [M] to the same unit. Sett, Brawler and Peak Guardian do check buff_count == 0 first.

name: King's Edict
summary: The opponent's choice is replaced by a lowest-Might heuristic.
detail: The opponent should choose which unit the caster doesn't control is killed. The code auto-picks the opponent's lowest-Might unit, which ignores keywords and abilities.

name: Leona, Determined
summary: 'Stun an enemy unit here' can target an enemy unit at any battlefield.
detail: TargetRequirements only has must_be_at_battlefield; there is no way to say 'same battlefield as the source', and the card does not override enumerateLegalTargets. Leona can therefore stun an enemy at the other battlefield.

name: Baited Hook
summary: The cost uses recycle_self (puts Baited Hook into the Main Deck) and never charges the [Y] power.
detail: Official cost is [1][Y],[E]. The engine_text '[C]' was read as 'recycle this', so activating recycles the gear itself (game_engine.cpp:1463) and charges no Order power.

name: Baited Hook
summary: 'You may' play the unit is forced: if any eligible unit exists, one is always played.
detail: pickTarget over the eligible units offers no decline option, so the player can't keep all five cards and recycle them.

name: Darius, Executioner
summary: 'Other friendly units have +1 [M] here' is not implemented.
detail: Only the Legion ready trigger exists. There is no applyPassiveAura override, and nothing in src/engine handles Darius, so friendly units at his battlefield never get the +1 [M]. Garen, Commander (0311) shows the aura pattern that is needed.

name: Divine Judgment
summary: Units and gear on the board are recycled with recycleCards, which skips the leave-board handling: tokens go into the main deck and attachments are left behind.
detail: recycleCards only resets zone and location and inserts into the owner's main deck. Tokens should cease to exist (CR 183.1) but end up in the deck. Gear attached to a recycled unit keeps a stale attached_to, and no leave-board cleanup runs. In addition, which 2 of each category to keep (highest Might for units, first-found for gear, runes and hand) is a heuristic instead of each player's choice (simplification).

name: Viktor, Leader
summary: The 'non-Recruit' filter is not applied, so a Recruit dying makes another Recruit.
detail: The code comment says the dead unit can't be identified, but trigger_manager.cpp:671 passes the dead unit as the subject (chain.resuming->triggering_subject). The card could check that unit's 'Recruit' tag. As written, every friendly Recruit token that dies makes a new Recruit.

name: Icathian Rain
summary: All six 'Deal 2 to a unit' instances hit the same single target.
detail: Each line is a separate 'deal 2 to a unit' and can be aimed at a different unit. The code deals 2 six times to targets[0], so once that unit dies the remaining damage is wasted.

name: Stormbringer
summary: The battlefield is the one with the lowest-id enemy unit rather than the player's choice, and the unit does not move if no battlefield has enemies.
detail: The text lets the player choose a battlefield, deal damage to all enemy units there, then move the unit there. The code anchors on enemy_at_bf.front(), which can be the wrong battlefield. When no enemy unit is at any battlefield it returns early without moving the chosen unit, although the move should still happen.

name: Loose Cannon
summary: Draws 1 every Beginning Phase, ignoring the 'one or fewer cards in hand' condition.
detail: Text says to draw 1 only if you have one or fewer cards in hand. onTrigger calls drawCards unconditionally, with no hand-size check and no triggerCondition override, so the legend draws an extra card every turn.

name: Super Mega Death Rocket!
summary: 'When you conquer, you may discard 1 to return this from your trash to your hand' is not implemented.
detail: The code says this is an engine gap (conquer triggers are not scanned in the trash). No COVERAGE-OK handling exists in src/engine.

name: Noxian Guillotine
summary: Without Legion, 'Kill it the next time it takes damage this turn' sets a counter that nothing reads.
detail: The code writes card_counters["__kill_on_next_damage_this_turn"], but grep finds no engine or executor code that reads it. Without Legion the spell therefore does nothing; only the Legion immediate kill works.

name: Nine-Tailed Fox
summary: Stub: the only ability is not implemented.
detail: 'When an enemy unit attacks a battlefield you control, give it -1 [M] this turn, to a minimum of 1' has no triggerType and no onTrigger, and the engine has no COVERAGE-OK handling for it. The legend does nothing.

name: Fox-Fire
summary: Units are killed greedily from lowest Might, on both sides, instead of the units the player chooses.
detail: The code collects all units at the battlefield regardless of controller and kills the lowest-Might ones first while the total stays at 4 or less. The caster's own small units are killed ahead of enemy targets, and the player cannot choose which units to kill.

name: Dragon's Rage
summary: The destination and the second enemy unit are picked automatically; the fallback can 'move' the unit to the battlefield it is already at.
detail: The caster should choose where the enemy unit moves and which other enemy unit at that destination fights it. The code takes the first battlefield with another enemy unit and the first such unit. With no clash target it moves the unit to battlefields.front(), which may be its current battlefield.

name: Unforgiven
summary: Can only move a unit to base, not from base to a battlefield.
detail: Text says 'Move a friendly unit to or from your base.' onActivate always calls moveToBase, so it can't move a unit out of base. engine_text also says 'its base' where the official text says 'your base'.

name: Last Breath
summary: Only readies the unit; the 'deals damage equal to its Might to an enemy unit at a battlefield' clause is missing.
detail: onResolve only calls readyObject(targets[0]). No enemy target is chosen and no damage is dealt, and no engine coverage exists.

name: Zenith Blade
summary: The friendly unit that moves is the first one found in map order, not the player's choice.
detail: After the yes/no, the code moves the first friendly unit not already at that battlefield. The player should choose which unit moves.

name: Swift Scout
summary: 'You may pay [1] to hide a card with [Hidden] instead of [A]' is not implemented.
detail: The code comment marks it as an ENGINE GAP. Only the Teemo-to-hand ability works.

name: Guerilla Warfare
summary: 'You can hide cards ignoring costs this turn' is not implemented, and the returned cards are auto-picked.
detail: A TODO marks the hide-cost clause as an engine gap. The 'up to two' [Hidden] cards are the two most recently trashed, not the player's choice, and returning them is not optional.

name: Bullet Time
summary: Maximum X counts only exhausted runes in base; ready runes (and floating power) can also pay [A].
detail: Power is paid by recycling runes, ready or exhausted. The code caps X at the number of exhausted runes and recycles only those, which understates the maximum X and bypasses the normal payment path.

name: The Boss
summary: Death replacement never charges the [A] cost and is applied automatically instead of as a 'may'.
detail: Text says 'you may pay [A] and exhaust me'. applyReplacement always applies when The Boss is ready (no player choice) and pays no power, so the save is free and forced, which can waste the legend's exhaust.

name: Showstopper
summary: The target is not restricted to units in your base, and the destination battlefield is picked automatically.
detail: TargetRequirements is friendly unit only, so units already at a battlefield are legal targets (they get buffed and moved between battlefields). The destination should be the player's choice but is the first controlled battlefield, otherwise battlefields.front() (simplification).

name: Fortified Position
summary: 'Choose a unit' is restricted to the defending player's units anywhere on board.
detail: The text lets the player choose any unit. The code offers only friendly units, including those not at this battlefield. Practically equivalent, since Shield only matters for defenders here. The Shield is granted via giveTemporaryKeyword (turn-long), not 'this combat'.

name: Hallowed Tomb
summary: The 'you may' is forced, and any champion unit in the trash is returned instead of specifically the Chosen Champion.
detail: There is no confirmOptional, so the return always happens. The loop takes the first unit with isChampion() in the trash, which may not be the player's Chosen Champion (the engine never records which object started in the Champion Zone).

name: Monastery of Hirana
summary: The engine auto-picks the first buffed friendly unit to spend the buff from, and the cost is paid at resolution, not at finalization.
detail: 'Spend a buff' is the player's choice of which buffed unit. The code takes the first one in map order. The buff is also removed after finalizingChoices, not under costDueNow.

name: Navori Fighting Pit
summary: Trigger never buffs: it reads targets[0], but triggered abilities are queued with no targets.
detail: TriggerManager::fireTrigger calls chain_.addAbility(source, controller, def) with no targets, and chooseTargetsAtFinalize only runs runFinalizePass for triggers (getTargetRequirements is never consulted for them). So targets is always empty and 'buff a unit here' never happens. Its TargetRequirements also allow any battlefield, not just 'here'. It needs pickTarget over units at this battlefield, plus kFinalizeTrigger.

name: Sigil of the Storm
summary: The engine recycles the first rune it finds (map order) instead of letting the player choose which rune.
detail: The newest text is 'recycle one of your runes', without the old 'doesn't choose anything' wording. The code picks an arbitrary rune, ready or exhausted, which can matter for available resources.

name: The Candlelit Sanctum
summary: Uses predict(2), which never lets the player choose the order of kept cards and in fact reverses them.
detail: The text says 'Put those you don't [recycle] back in any order'. EffectExecutor::predict pushes kept cards back in peek order, so the original top card ends up second, and no ordering choice is offered.

name: The Dreaming Tree
summary: Also triggers when an ABILITY chooses a friendly unit here, but the text says 'with a spell'. Its comment claiming the trigger is inert is stale.
detail: The 'chosen_by_controller' event is emitted from ChainManager::addSpell, ChainManager::addAbility (chain_manager.cpp:138) and resolve-time choices (game_engine.cpp:1273). TriggerManager maps all of them to WhenAFriendlyUnitChosenHere, so abilities also draw a card. The card is tournament-banned, so impact is low.

name: Void Gate
summary: Implemented per the old wording (+1 damage taken by units here). The official text is 'spells and abilities affecting units here each deal 1 Bonus Damage'.
detail: Under the official wording, a spell that affects a unit here gets +1 Bonus Damage on each instance it deals, possibly including damage to units elsewhere. The code only adds bonus_damage_taken to units at this battlefield.
errata_note: Errata 2025-10-21: 'deal 1 Bonus Damage to units here' is the current text and matches the code.

name: Daughter of the Void
summary: 'Use only to play spells' restriction is not enforced on the added power.
detail: The ability adds plain universal power with addFloatingUniversalPower, which can pay for units, gear and abilities. The executor has no spell-only power pool.

name: Relentless Storm
summary: Triggers on any unit play while any friendly Mighty unit is on board, not only when the played unit is Mighty.
detail: The legend WhenYouPlayAUnit sweep passes no subject, so the card scans the board for any friendly unit with 5+ Might. Playing a 1-Might unit while you already control a Mighty unit lets you exhaust to channel a rune.

name: Radiant Dawn
summary: Buffs the first friendly unit in map order instead of letting the player choose.
detail: Text says 'buff a friendly unit'. Code buffs the first on-board friendly unit it finds, even if that unit already has a buff (which wastes the buff).

name: Flash
summary: 'Up to 2' is forced to exactly 2 when 2 or more units are eligible.
detail: pickTargetPair has no decline option, so the player cannot move just one unit (the code's GAP comment says so).

name: Lux, Crownguard
summary: The 2 energy added is not restricted to spells.
detail: The text says '[Add] [2]. Use only to play spells.' The code adds 2 unrestricted floating energy that can pay for units, gear or abilities. The code comment acknowledges this.

name: Recruit the Vanguard
summary: All four Recruit tokens always go to base.
detail: The text lets them be played to base or to battlefields you control. The code hard-codes base, so the player cannot reinforce a held battlefield.

name: Dark Child - Starter
summary: The runes to ready are the first exhausted runes in map order, not chosen by the player.
detail: Ready 2 runes: runes differ by domain, but code readies the first two exhausted runes it finds.

name: Tibbers
summary: Deals 3 to every unit on the board, including units in bases, instead of only units at battlefields.
detail: The text says 'deal 3 to all units at battlefields.' The filter only checks location.has_value(), so units in both bases are hit. That includes Tibbers itself when it is played to base, and base units with 3 or less might die.

name: Might of Demacia - Starter
summary: 'That battlefield' is approximated as any battlefield scored this turn.
detail: The trigger has no conquered-battlefield id, so the code checks every battlefield in battlefields_scored_this_turn (including holds and earlier conquers). It can draw 2 on a conquer elsewhere if an earlier scored battlefield still has 4+ friendly units.

name: Decisive Strike
summary: Gives +2 to one targeted friendly unit instead of all friendly units.
detail: The text says 'Give friendly units +2 [M] this turn' with no target. The code uses a count=1 friendly target and buffs only targets[0].

name: Against the Odds
summary: Gives a flat +2 instead of +2 for each enemy unit at that battlefield.
detail: onResolve calls giveTemporaryMight(targets[0], 2) without counting the enemy units at the target's battlefield.

name: Armed Assailant
summary: Weaponmaster via WeaponmasterUnit base: forced (no 'may'), auto-picks the first Equipment found, and equips for free instead of Equip cost minus [A].
detail: Text: 'you may [Equip] one of your Equipment to me for [A] less'. weaponmaster_base.h onTrigger always equips the first Equipment in map order (steals it even from another friendly unit), with no confirm or pick, and charges nothing even if the Equip cost exceeds [A]. Also no objectExists(ctx.source) check before getObject(ctx.source). Same base is used by Combat Chef (414), Veteran Poro (421/779), Master Bingwen, Yone, Riven.

name: Blood Rush
summary: Official text grants [Assault 2] permanently; the engine text and code make it 'this turn'.
detail: The gallery text is 'Give a unit [Assault 2].' with no duration. engine_text adds 'this turn' and the code uses giveTemporaryKeyword. No errata was found in errata/ or rules/patch-notes.

name: Bushwhack
summary: Readies the friendly units already on the board instead of making units entering later this turn enter ready.
detail: 'Friendly units enter ready this turn' affects future plays. The code readies every exhausted friendly unit now, a strong effect the card does not have, and does nothing for units played afterwards.

name: Detonate
summary: 'Its controller draws 2' is missing.
detail: onResolve only kills the gear. No draw happens for the gear's controller.

name: Gem Jammer
summary: Trigger relies on `targets`, but triggered abilities are added to the chain with empty targets, so the Ganking grant never happens.
detail: TriggerManager::fireTrigger -> chain_.addAbility(source, controller, def_id) passes no targets, and getTargetRequirements() is only consulted for spells/activated abilities; onTrigger does `if (!targets.empty())` so it is a no-op. Needs pickTarget + kFinalizeTrigger. Additionally def sets d.keywords.set(Keyword::Ganking) on Gem Jammer itself, which the printed card does not have (text-mismatch: Gem Jammer permanently has Ganking).

name: Sentinel Adept
summary: Weaponmaster equip is always free rather than Equip cost minus [A].
detail: Text says Equip 'for [A] less'; code attaches with no payment, so Equipment whose Equip cost exceeds [A] (or has an energy component) is equipped free. Optional + pick are correctly implemented.

name: Minotaur Reckoner
summary: cant_move_to_base is stamped on every unit but never cleared, so the restriction persists forever after Minotaur leaves the board.
detail: applyPassiveAura sets obj.cant_move_to_base = true; grep shows nothing resets it in recalculateAuras (only Determined Sentry sets it). Units that were on board keep 'can't move to base' permanently, including the opponent's. Also only the move-action check (game_engine.cpp:2659) reads the flag, so card effects that move units to base are not blocked.

name: Recurve Bow
summary: The 2 damage goes to the first enemy unit found at the battlefield; the player doesn't choose.
detail: Text: 'deal 2 to an enemy unit here'. Code iterates state.objects and damages the first enemy unit there (object-map order), so the player can't choose the target, which changes outcomes.

name: Assembly Rig
summary: The unit recycled from trash as the cost is picked automatically (the most recent one), and the cost is paid at resolution.
detail: The player should choose which unit to recycle. The choice can matter for later trash-play effects.

name: Draven, Vanquisher
summary: The pay-[R] option is offered only if a READY Fury rune is at base, though payOnePower can also pay from pooled power or exhausted Fury runes.
detail: has_fury_power skips exhausted runes and ignores rune_pool power; recycling an exhausted rune for power is legal and payOnePower prefers exhausted runes. Player is wrongly denied the +2 [M] option in those states.

name: Piercing Light
summary: must_be_at_battlefield appears to apply to both targets, but the second target ('up to one other unit') may be anywhere.
detail: TargetRequirements is shared by both picks (count=2, must_be_at_battlefield=true). If the generator applies it to every pick, units in base cannot be the second target. Not verified in the action generator.

name: Rumble, Hotheaded
summary: The unit to recycle and the Mech to play are auto-picked (first found) instead of chosen by the player, and the unit is recycled even if the Mech then cannot be paid for.
detail: find_recyclable returns the first friendly unit in map order (its Might determines the cost reduction) and find_trash_mech the most recent Mech in trash; neither is a player choice. recycleCards runs before canPlayPayingCost, so a failed payment still loses the recycled unit.

name: Ribbon Dancer
summary: Trigger relies on `targets`, which are always empty for triggered abilities, so the +1 [M] is never given; also does not exclude itself ('another').
detail: fireTrigger adds the ability with no targets and nothing fills them from getTargetRequirements for triggers; onTrigger does `if (!targets.empty())`, a no-op. TargetRequirements also has no exclude-self, so even if targets were filled Ribbon Dancer could pick itself.

name: Thwonk!
summary: Can stun any unit, not only an attacking unit.
detail: TargetRequirements is just must_be_unit, and there is no enumerateLegalTargets override filtering on combat_designation==Attacker. The spell can be played outside combat on any unit.

name: Legion Quartermaster
summary: Mandatory additional cost (return a friendly gear) is paid as a WhenYouPlayMe trigger after the unit enters rather than as a cost.
detail: Documented approximation: the bounce goes on the chain as a trigger and can be responded to; it also means the cost is skipped if the trigger fizzles, and the bounced gear could be one played to satisfy nothing. Playability gating via hasLegalTargets is correct.

name: Poro Snax
summary: 'Kill this' is modeled as recycle_self, so the gear goes to the bottom of the Main Deck instead of dying, and the [G] power is never charged.
detail: Cost should be [1][G],[E], kill this. Code uses {.exhaust, .energy=1, .recycle_self}. Poro Snax is recycled into the deck (no trash, no death triggers), and the Calm power is never paid, although ActivationCost supports power/power_domain.

name: Aphelios, Exalted
summary: 'Ready 2 runes' auto-picks the first two exhausted runes in map order instead of letting the player choose.
detail: Rune domains differ, so which runes get readied can matter. Everything else (mode mask, finalization) looks correct.

name: Azir, Ascendant
summary: The 'you may attach one of its Equipment' step cannot be declined: pickTargetPair always attaches one if the chosen unit has gear.
detail: Documented GAP. Also the once-per-turn flag is set only on resolution, so a second activation could be put on the chain before the first resolves.

name: Jax, Unmatched
summary: Def sets Keyword::Reaction (and QuickDraw) on Jax himself, so the unit can be played at Reaction speed; printed Jax has only Deflect.
detail: Those keywords come from Quick-Draw's reminder text and belong on Equipment, not Jax. Also the aura grants Quick-Draw to owned Equipment in every zone, while the official text is 'Each Equipment in your hand has [Quick-Draw]' (text-mismatch: Equipment played from trash or another zone also gets Reaction plus auto-attach).
errata_note: Errata 2026-01-12: 'Your Equipment everywhere have [Quick-Draw]' — the every-zone aura is correct; only the Reaction/QuickDraw keywords on Jax himself are a bug.

name: Needlessly Large Yordle
summary: Only the [2] energy part of the '[2][G] less per hold point' discount is applied; the [G] power reduction is missing.
detail: Documented ESCALATE gap: selfCostReduction lowers energy only, so the 3 printed power is always charged in full. (The comment calls [G] Order, but the card is Calm, which is correct for [G].)

name: Irelia, Fervent
summary: 'When you choose me' is wired to WhenYouChooseAFriendlyUnit, which fires on every OTHER friendly unit being chosen and never on Irelia herself.
detail: trigger_manager.cpp:1110 skips the chosen object (`id == e.object`) when collecting watchers, and Irelia has no triggerCondition to restrict the subject to herself. So she gets +1 [M] whenever you choose another friendly unit, and gets nothing when you choose her. The ready half (WhenIAmReadied) is fine.

name: Ornn, Blacksmith
summary: 'You may reveal a gear and draw it' always takes the first gear among the top 4, with no choice of gear and no option to decline.
detail: When several gears are revealed the player should pick one (and may take none). Code drafts the first gear in deck order.

name: Svellsongur
summary: The 'copy that unit's text' clause is not implemented; the card is a plain equip.
detail: Only onEquip (standardEquip [1][G]) is implemented. Nothing copies the bearer's text/abilities onto the equipment, and there is no engine COVERAGE-OK handling.

name: Aspiring Engineer
summary: Implements the wrong effect (bounce a friendly gear on board), and since trigger targets are always empty it does nothing at all.
detail: Text: 'return a gear from your trash to your hand'. Code calls bounceToHand(targets[0]) on a must_be_friendly on-board gear, but triggered abilities are added with empty targets, so the branch never runs. It should pick a gear from the controller's trash and move it to hand.

name: Bubble Bot
summary: Which friendly Mech to ready is auto-picked (first exhausted one found) rather than chosen by the player.
detail: Matters when several Mechs are exhausted (e.g. one at a battlefield vs one at base). Low impact.

name: Breakneck Mech
summary: 'Enter ready if you control another Mech' skips every object with Breakneck Mech's def id, so a second copy of Breakneck Mech already on board does not count.
detail: Should exclude only this object (by id), not all copies. Direwing (416) has the same pattern for 'another Dragon'.

name: Experimental Hexplate
summary: 'I am a Mech' is not implemented: the equipped unit never gains the Mech tag.
detail: The class is a bare SimpleEquipGear. The tag grant to the bearer isn't modeled, so Mech-synergy cards don't see it.

name: Temporal Portal
summary: The effect is a stub: no Repeat grant to the next spell.
detail: onActivate only logs, as the ESCALATE note admits. The [A] cost is also encoded as Mind power (power_domain=Mind) instead of power_any_domain=true, so any-domain power can't pay it. The gear's own CardDef also sets Keyword::Repeat (line 59), which is meaningless on a gear.

name: Card Sharp
summary: The opponent's 'may play a Gold token' is always accepted, which always gives the controller the extra Gold token; the opponent never decides.
detail: Text: 'you and each opponent may play a Gold gear token exhausted. For each opponent who did, you play a Gold gear token.' The opponent faces a real trade-off (gives you a Gold too), but code forces both optional plays and always creates the payoff token.

name: Hextech Anomaly
summary: The ability is not flagged [Reaction] (isReactionAbility is not overridden), so it can't be used in closed state or on the opponent's turn.
detail: Text: '[E]: [Reaction] — Pay any amount of [A]...'. Code overrides isActionAbility()=false but not isReactionAbility(), so the default activatedAbilities() sets is_reaction=false and the reaction-timing generator (game_engine.cpp ~3210) skips it. The Seals and Ancient Henge set isReactionAbility()=true.

name: Jayce, Man of Progress
summary: The friendly gear is killed before the pickTarget suspension, so on resume onTrigger reruns and kills a second friendly gear; the gear to kill is also auto-picked.
detail: killObject(gear) runs, then pickTarget suspends and returns; the resume calls onTrigger again, where confirmOptional returns the stored yes and findFriendlyGear returns the next friendly gear, which is killed too. The killed gear is the first in map order, not a player choice. The follow-up play uses playIgnoringCost, so the gear's Power cost is skipped (it should be playPayingCost with ignore_energy), and the play happens immediately instead of granting a 'this turn' permission, with no way to decline it.

name: Ornn, Forge God
summary: Weaponmaster is forced, auto-picks the first friendly Equipment (stealing it from another unit), and is free instead of Equip cost minus [A].
detail: Same hand-rolled logic as WeaponmasterUnit: no 'may', no choice, no payment. Jax, Unrelenting (440) shows the faithful pattern.

name: The Zero Drive
summary: The replay ability charges only [3] energy; the [B] power is never paid.
detail: getActivationCost returns {.energy=3}. The comment calls this an engine limitation, but ActivationCost has power/power_domain, which payActivationResources pays.

name: The Zero Drive
summary: '[Deathknell] — Banish me' is a death replacement, so the bearer never actually dies.
detail: Deathknell is a 'when I die' trigger: the unit should die (firing its own Deathknell and 'when a friendly unit dies' triggers) and then be banished. applyReplacement returns true, so killUnit/killObject skip the death entirely and no death triggers fire.

name: Buhru Captain
summary: The 'or buff me' option is missing; the trigger always draws 1.
detail: Text: 'you may draw 1 or buff me'. Code unconditionally draws, with no mode choice (pickMode) and no buff path.

name: Direwing
summary: Another Direwing already on board is not counted as 'another Dragon' because all objects with this def id are skipped.
detail: entersReadyOnPlay skips by card_def_id instead of by the entering object's id, so a controlled Direwing is wrongly excluded.

name: Yordle Explorer
summary: Finds the played card by scanning the chain, but the played card is gone by the time the trigger resolves, so it misses or reads an unrelated chain item.
detail: Permanents are erased from the chain when they resolve on finalize (chain_manager.cpp:234), and spell play triggers fire from onSpellResolved after the spell has left the chain. So unit and gear plays never draw, and a spell play reads whatever spell is lower on the chain, if any. It should use the trigger's triggering_subject (if fired with a subject) or a captured def id.

name: Fae Dragon
summary: 'When you spend a buff, play a Gold gear token exhausted' is not implemented.
detail: Documented ENGINE GAP: there is no spend-buff trigger. Also, with more than 4 unbuffed friendly units, the 'up to four' are auto-picked in map order (minor simplification).

name: Petricite Monument
summary: The gear itself carries Keyword::Deflect, though only friendly units should have it.
detail: 'Friendly units have [Deflect]' is applied correctly via the aura, but d.keywords.set(Deflect) also makes opponents pay [A] to choose the Monument itself.

name: Strike Down
summary: Detaches the first Equipment found rather than letting the player choose which one.
detail: Text says 'detach an Equipment from it'. When a unit carries several Equipment, which one comes off is a player choice; code always picks the first attachment.

name: Akshan, Mischievous
summary: The optional [O][O] cost is charged as Order power; [O] is Body (Akshan is a Body card), so the cost needs the wrong domain.
detail: Other [O] costs use Domain::Body (e.g. Legion Marauder 0861, Jaull-Fish's Accelerate). Also: the enemy gear to steal is auto-picked (first enemy gear found, line 37) instead of chosen, and the printed [Weaponmaster] ability has no trigger at all (missing clause): only the keyword bit is set.

name: Fiora, Peerless
summary: 'Double my Might this combat' is applied as temporary Might until end of turn, not end of combat.
detail: giveTemporaryMight lasts the turn, so after this combat ends Fiora keeps the doubled Might for any later effect or combat that turn.

name: Here to Help
summary: Destination is the first controlled battlefield chosen heuristically, falling back to base, and the 'you may' has no decline option.
detail: Text says play a unit to a battlefield you control. Code picks the first controlled battlefield without asking, and plays to base when the player controls none, which the text does not allow. The choice list holds only units, so the optional play cannot be declined.

name: Kato the Arm
summary: Code excludes Kato himself ('another friendly unit'), but the official text is 'give a friendly unit my keywords and +[M]'.
detail: Under the gallery text Kato can target himself (doubling his Might this turn); the engine_text and code say 'another'. Granted keywords also use value 0 via giveTemporaryKeyword, so a granted Deflect may carry no Deflect value.

name: Lucian, Merciless
summary: Weaponmaster is forced, auto-picks the first Equipment, and equips free.
detail: Same issue as WeaponmasterUnit: no 'may', no gear choice, no Equip cost minus [A] payment. The once-per-turn conquer ready is correct.

name: Sivir, Ambitious
summary: The conquer payoff is a stub (logs only), even though the engine now tracks excess combat damage.
detail: PlayerState::excess_combat_damage / last_combat_attacker exist (game_state.h:237, set at game_engine.cpp:2471, helper in card_helpers.h:89), so 'if you assigned 5+ excess damage, you may deal that much to an enemy unit' is now implementable but does nothing.

name: Called Shot
summary: The chosen card is moved to hand by hand-editing zones, not through drawCards, so it is not a draw.
detail: Text says 'Draw one'. Code erases the card from main_deck and pushes it into hand directly. No draw event is emitted, so 'when you draw' triggers and draw counters miss it.

name: Fae Porter
summary: [P] payment is not checked at finalization and is paid at resolution.
detail: still_legal only checks for a movable unit, not whether [P] is payable; the player can accept and pick a target, then payOnePower fails at resolution and nothing happens. The '[cost] to [effect]' payment should be decided and paid at finalization (costDueNow), like Vayne, Hunter.

name: Master Bingwen
summary: Weaponmaster attaches the first Equipment for free, always, with no player choice.
detail: Text: 'you may [Equip] one of your Equipment to me for [A] less'. WeaponmasterUnit::onTrigger picks the first Equipment found, makes the equip mandatory and pays nothing at all (the equip cost minus [A], not zero). This changes outcomes for Equipment whose equip cost is above [A], and it can steal Equipment from another unit against the player's wishes.

name: Overzealous Fan
summary: Attacker is returned to its owner's hand, but the text says to move it to its base.
detail: Text: 'kill me to move an attacking unit to its base'. The code calls ctx.executor.bounceToHand(attacker), which sends the card to hand (a much stronger effect) instead of recalling it to base (moveToBase). It also only considers the single captured attacker rather than letting the player choose any attacking unit.

name: Ancient Warmonger
summary: Assault is off by one: printed assault_value=1 plus an aura worth the enemy count.
detail: def sets d.assault_value = 1, which GameObject::recomputeMight adds whenever the unit is an attacker, and applyPassiveAura also adds might_bonus = enemies while attacking. Total attacking bonus = enemies + 1 (for example +1 when attacking an empty battlefield, where the text gives +0). assault_value should be 0, keeping the Assault keyword for presence only.

name: Beast Below
summary: Target requirements set both must_be_enemy and must_be_friendly, so no unit is ever a legal target and nothing is returned.
detail: Card::legal-target filtering (card.cpp:646-647) rejects every object under both flags, so the trigger has no legal target. Even if fixed, onTrigger returns only targets[0], while the text returns another friendly unit AND an enemy unit (two bounces). The whole effect is effectively missing.

name: Hard Bargain
summary: The opponent's ability to pay [2] counts only ready runes at base and pays by exhausting two runes, ignoring rune-pool energy and other payment sources.
detail: Text says 'unless its controller pays [2]'. Code checks ready_runes >= 2 and exhausts the first two runes, with no agent choice of which runes. Energy already in the pool is ignored, so the spell can be countered when the controller could have paid.

name: Harpoon Squad
summary: 'from a battlefield' qualifier is ignored; a move from base also gives +2 [M].
detail: The text gives +2 [M] only when moving FROM a battlefield. The code uses WhenIMove and grants on any move, including the common base-to-battlefield attack move. That gives +2 [M] on attacks where the text gives nothing, which changes combat outcomes. The comment acknowledges this.

name: Windsinger
summary: Keyword::Hidden is not set, so the card can never be hidden.
detail: The engine offers the hide action only for cards with keywords.has(Keyword::Hidden) (game_engine.cpp ~2874). Windsinger's def sets no keywords, and its ability_text reads 'Hidden (' without brackets. The [Hidden] line is therefore non-functional. Compare Mischievous Marai, which sets d.keywords.set(Keyword::Hidden).

name: Edge of Night
summary: On play from facedown it attaches to the first friendly unit found here; the player doesn't choose.
detail: Text: 'attach it to a unit you control here'. Code loops over state.objects and attaches to the first match.

name: Fizz, Trickster
summary: The spell to replay is auto-picked (most recent eligible spell in trash) instead of chosen by the player.
detail: Text: 'you may play a spell from your trash with Energy cost no more than [3]'. find_spell returns the last eligible trash spell, so the player cannot choose which spell to play. The spell's targets and choices come from the normal play path.

name: Irelia, Graceful
summary: Discount applies only to play-time-targeted spells and is modeled as a flat value of 1.
detail: The code comment states that spells choosing their targets at chain time (needsPlayTimeTarget/pickTarget) get no discount, because the cost is already paid by then. The '[1] or [A]' alternative (reduce power instead of energy) depends on how transient_play_discount is consumed. This is not verified here.

name: Vex, Cheerless
summary: Permanent CostModifiers are pushed on every aura recalculation and never removed, so they accumulate without bound and outlive Vex.
detail: applyPassiveAura pushes two CostModifiers with this_turn_only=false. recalculateAuras never clears PlayerState::cost_modifiers: they are only erased at turn end (this_turn_only) or when consumed as one-shots. Every cleanup adds another -1/+1 pair, so enemy costs grow without limit during any combat, and the modifiers remain after Vex leaves play. The same pattern appears in Eager Apprentice, Herald of Scales and Ornn's Forge, which are outside this batch.

name: Vex, Cheerless
summary: Power component missing, the modifier is not limited to spells, and 'while I'm in combat' is treated as 'any combat'.
detail: The text is '[1][A] less / [1][A] more' for SPELLS while VEX is in combat. The code sets only energy_reduction/energy_increase (no power), uses no spell-only filter (so units and gear are also discounted or taxed), and combat_active_only checks whether any battlefield has combat, not whether Vex is an attacker or defender.

name: Ezreal, Prodigy
summary: 'Optional additional costs you pay cost [1] or [A] less' is not implemented.
detail: Only the play trigger (discard 1, then draw 2) exists. There is no cost-reduction hook for optional additional costs (Accelerate and similar) in the card, and nothing in src/engine references Ezreal.

name: Last Rites
summary: The unit from trash is played for free; 'You still pay its costs' is ignored.
detail: The code calls playIgnoringCost and admits it is a gap. Hold/conquer gives a free unit of any cost from trash, which changes outcomes a lot. The 2 recycled trash cards for the equip cost are also auto-picked (back of trash), and the 'you may' is not decided at finalization (no choicesAtFinalization).

name: Eye of the Herald
summary: The Recruit token is created ready (enter_ready=true); played units enter exhausted.
detail: Text: 'play a 1 [M] Recruit unit token here'. Nothing says it enters ready (CR 143.4). Other token makers in the batch (Vanguard Armory, Assembly Rig) pass enter_ready=false.

name: Zaun Punk
summary: The 'kill a friendly gear' additional cost is moved from play time into the play trigger.
detail: The cost is paid at trigger resolution instead of as an additional cost while playing. If the trigger is countered or the gear leaves before resolution, the cost and effect interact differently from the printed timing. The outcome is usually the same.

name: Glasc Mixologist
summary: Only the energy cost is checked (<= [3]); the 'no more than [A]' (power cost <= 1) restriction is missing.
detail: eligibleTrashUnits filters on energy_cost > 3 only, so a unit with energy <= 3 but power cost >= 2 can be played for free, which the text forbids.

name: Rally the Troops
summary: The 'when a friendly unit is played this turn, buff it' rider is not implemented. Only Draw 1 runs.
detail: The comment documents an ENGINE GAP. onResolve only calls drawCards(1). The rest-of-turn buff on each friendly unit played is missing.

name: Vanguard Armory
summary: All three Recruit tokens always go to base; the player can't choose locations.
detail: Text: '(You may play them to different locations.)'. Code hardcodes BaseLocation for all three.

name: Altar of Memories
summary: The '__altar_drew' guard counter is never cleared, so after the first use Altar never exhausts or draws again.
detail: card_counters['__altar_drew']=1 is set on the gear permanently (no other reference in the repo). Every later trigger skips exhaust+draw and still makes the player put a hand card on the deck, a pure downside with no cost paid. It should use resume_data, or clear the counter at the end.

name: Rek'Sai, Swarm Queen
summary: Implements the older 'banish one, then play it' wording; a card that can't be paid for stays banished, and 'you may play it here' is forced.
detail: Official text: 'You may play one. Then recycle the rest. If the played card is a unit, you may play it here.' The code first banishes the picked card. If canPlayPayingCost fails, the card stays in banishment instead of being recycled with the rest. A unit is always placed at Rek'Sai's battlefield with no base option.
errata_note: Errata 2026-01-12: 'You may banish one, then play it'.

name: Xin Zhao, Vigilant
summary: 'other units' is filtered by card def id, so a second Xin Zhao, Vigilant in base is not counted.
detail: entersReadyOnPlay skips every object with this card_def_id rather than only the entering object. Another copy of Xin Zhao in base would wrongly not count toward the 'two or more other units' requirement.

name: Azir, Sovereign
summary: 'you may move any number of your token units' always moves all of them.
detail: No player choice: every friendly token unit not already at the battlefield is moved. This includes tokens defending elsewhere, which the player might want to keep there.

name: Blade of the Ruined King
summary: The friendly unit killed as the equip cost is auto-picked (the first legal one); the player doesn't choose.
detail: onEquip runs directly from payAndQueueAbility with no chain item resuming, so pickTarget takes its no-chain branch and returns legal_targets.front(). Which friendly unit dies is effectively arbitrary (object-map order).

name: Fiora, Worthy
summary: The [Y] payment is not checked at finalization and is made at resolution.
detail: still_legal does not check that [Y] is payable. The cost is paid at resolution via payOnePower instead of at finalization under costDueNow, unlike the Vayne pattern.

name: Danger Zone
summary: Gives +1 [M] to a single targeted friendly unit, not to all of your Mechs.
detail: Text says 'Give your Mechs +1 [M] this turn'. Code targets one friendly unit of any tag (count=1, must_be_friendly) and buffs only that unit. It neither filters on the Mech tag nor affects every Mech.

name: Relentless Pursuit
summary: The 'When I conquer, you may move me to my base' grant is a no-op. The move destination and the Equipment attach are heuristics, and the optional attach is forced.
detail: Code moves the unit only to the first battlefield where another friendly unit stands, with no player choice. Base, empty battlefields and enemy battlefields are never offered, and the unit does not move if no such battlefield exists. The first unattached friendly Equipment is attached automatically, though the text makes this optional and allows any Equipment, by editing fields directly. The conquer grant is not implemented.

name: Spinning Axe
summary: [Temporary] kills the Axe even while it is attached; the text says only if unattached.
detail: The engine's Temporary sweep (game_engine.cpp ~761) kills every Temporary gear the turn player controls with no attached_to check, and the card adds no override. Attached Spinning Axes die every Beginning Phase.

name: Spinning Axe
summary: UniversalEquipGear's [A] equip doesn't check that the cost can be paid, so the Axe equips for free with no rune at base.
detail: UniversalEquipGear::onEquip (gear/equip_base.h) recycles the first rune at base if there is one, but attaches even when none exists, and ignores floating power. Equip intents aren't gated on affordability (game_engine.cpp ~2858).

name: Void Rush
summary: Always takes the top card and banishes it before checking affordability, so an unaffordable card is lost to banishment. It also follows the old 'banish, then play' text.
detail: Official text: 'You may play one of them, reducing its cost by [2]. Draw any you did not play.' Code picks the first revealed card heuristically, which is effectively always the top one, and gives no choice and no decline. It removes the card from the deck and banishes it, and only then checks canPlayPayingCost. If that check fails, the card stays banished and is neither played nor drawn. The card is always played to base.
errata_note: Errata 2026-01-12: 'You may banish one, then play it ... Draw any you didn't banish' — banish-then-play is correct; the missing choice/decline remains.

name: Fire Below the Mountain
summary: 'Use only to play gear or use gear abilities' restriction is not enforced.
detail: Adds unrestricted universal power, as the trace message itself says ('not engine-enforced'), so it can pay for spells and units.

name: Forgefire Cape
summary: It inherits UniversalEquipGear's unchecked [A] equip cost, so it can be equipped for free with no runes.
detail: Same issue as Spinning Axe: UniversalEquipGear::onEquip attaches even when no rune can be recycled. Rabadon's Deathcrown instead uses the payOnePower-checked standardEquip(..., nullopt).

name: Rabadon's Deathcrown
summary: 'Your spells and abilities deal 3 Bonus Damage (while attached)' is not implemented.
detail: Only onEquip is overridden; there is no applyPassiveAura. The engine has a mechanism, PlayerState::bonus_damage_dealt (used by Annie, Fiery and reset each recalc), that an aura could raise by 3 while attached.

name: Arise!
summary: Engine text and code say 'Ready up to two'. The official text says 'ready two of them' (mandatory), and tokens always go to base.
detail: Code offers a 'ready no more' stop option, so readying is optional. The official text requires readying two. Token placement at base is a documented engine gap; the text allows base or a controlled battlefield.
errata_note: Errata 2026-01-12: 'Ready up to two of them'.

name: Prodigal Explorer
summary: Draw ability is missing its 'chosen enemy units/gear twice this turn' requirement and uses Action timing instead of Reaction.
detail: Text says '[E]: [Reaction] — Draw 1. Use only if you've chosen enemy units and/or gear twice this turn with spells or unit abilities.' Code has no canActivateAbility gate, so it is an unconditional [E]: draw 1, and it sets isActionAbility instead of isReactionAbility.

name: Arcane Shift
summary: The banish-and-replay step runs before pickTarget suspends, so it runs again on re-entry and the friendly unit is banished and replayed twice.
detail: pickTarget always publishes a choice when any enemy target exists and returns kInvalidId, so onResolve is re-entered from the top. targets[0] still exists after playIgnoringCost, which keeps the same id, so step 1 banishes and replays it again, firing play triggers twice. Separately, the owner's choice of play location is forced to base.

name: Battle Mistress
summary: The 'when you recycle a rune, exhaust me to play a Gold token' clause is not implemented.
detail: The code comment admits the first ability is not wired. Only the ready-me trigger exists.

name: Battle Mistress
summary: The WhenAnEnemyUnitDies trigger never reaches a legend, so 'ready me' never fires.
detail: TriggerManager (trigger_manager.cpp:664-677) only fires WhenAnEnemyUnitDies for objects with location.has_value(). Legend-zone objects have no location, and there is no fireLegendTrigger sweep for this trigger type, so both of Battle Mistress's abilities do nothing.

name: On the Hunt
