summary: Readies one targeted friendly unit instead of all of your units.
detail: Text says 'Ready your units.' Code has TargetRequirements count=1 and readies only targets[0].

name: Forge of the Fluft
summary: Only unattached Equipment can be chosen, so the ability can't move an Equipment that is already attached to another unit.
detail: The text says 'Attach an Equipment you control to a unit you control', with no unattached requirement. The code filters out gear with attached_to set.

name: Veiled Temple
summary: Conquer trigger is a no-op: it returns on empty targets, and triggers never get targets.
detail: 'You may ready a friendly gear' depends on getTargetRequirements, which the trigger pipeline ignores, so nothing is ever readied or detached. The 'you may' on the ready is also forced, and there is no choicesAtFinalization. It needs confirmOptional + pickTarget over friendly gear.

name: Ahri, Inquisitive
summary: 'an enemy unit here' is implemented as any enemy unit at any battlefield.
detail: TargetRequirements uses must_be_at_battlefield, which accepts enemy units at any battlefield, not only Ahri's battlefield. This allows -2 [M] on a unit elsewhere.

name: Bard, Mercurial
summary: Legend-exhaust cost is folded into the trigger; ALL units move to the FIRST open battlefield with no choice.
detail: Text: 'move any number of your units to an open battlefield'. The code moves every friendly unit, including ones defending other battlefields, to the first uncontrolled battlefield, and the player cannot choose which units or which battlefield. The additional cost is paid at resolution, not as a play cost.

name: Seal of Strength
summary: Adds Order ([Y]) power instead of Body ([O]) power.
detail: Text says [Add] [O] (Body; the card's own domain is Body, and other [O] cards like Hunter's Machete use Domain::Body). onActivate calls addFloatingPower(..., Domain::Order, 1), so the Seal produces the wrong domain.

name: Sett, Brawler
summary: 'Spend my buff' is not an activation cost: the ability is offered with no buff and the buff is spent at resolution.
detail: getActivationCost returns {}, so the engine offers the ability even when buff_count == 0 (resolving to nothing). The buff is removed at resolution rather than paid as the cost when the ability is activated.

name: Yone, Blademaster
summary: 'that was uncontrolled' condition not checked; the conquer damage fires on every conquer and auto-picks the first enemy unit in base.
detail: The code comment documents the missing condition: conquering an enemy-controlled battlefield also deals damage. The target is the first enemy base unit found in the map iteration, not a player choice. The Weaponmaster part repeats the free, forced, first-Equipment behavior described for Master Bingwen.

name: Darius, Executioner
summary: 'Other friendly units have +1 [M] here' is not implemented.
detail: The class has only the Legion ready trigger. There is no applyPassiveAura and the engine does not reference Darius, so the static +1 [M] aura for other friendly units at his location is missing.

name: Karma, Channeler
summary: Vision runs twice (Keyword::Vision is set AND a WhenYouPlayMe trigger repeats the peek), and the recycle-buff clause is missing even though WhenYouRecycle exists.
detail: TriggerManager (trigger_manager.cpp:317) already performs Vision for permanents with Keyword::Vision. The card's own trigger peeks and recycles a top spell a second time. 'When you recycle one or more cards, buff a friendly unit' is marked as an ENGINE GAP, but TriggerType::WhenYouRecycle exists and is used by Karma 235. The engine text also says 'to your Main Deck', which the official text does not.
errata_note: Errata 2025-10-21: 'to your Main Deck' is the current text.

name: Grandmaster at Arms
summary: Which Equipment to attach or move is picked automatically (first found), not chosen by the player.
detail: Both abilities say 'Attach a [detached/attached] Equipment you control'. onActivate takes the first matching Equipment in the objects map and only asks for the destination unit. The abilities are also offered when no eligible Equipment exists, which wastes the exhaust and [1].

name: Chem-Baroness
summary: Hold-only trigger is registered as WhenIConquerOrHold, so it also fires on conquer.
detail: Text: 'When you or an ally hold'. triggerType() returns WhenIConquerOrHold; TriggerManager::onScore fires that for both Conquer and Hold, while a dedicated WhenIHold legend trigger exists (used by Gloomist). Conquering wrongly offers a Gold token.

name: Chem-Baroness
summary: Second ability (Gold adds an additional [1] while within 3 of Victory Score) is not implemented.
detail: The code logs 'Gold-add bonus passive not modeled'; there is no applyPassiveAura and Gold (0326_gold.cpp onActivate) always adds exactly 1 [A] with no Chem-Baroness check anywhere in engine.

name: Prepared Neophyte
summary: Reads only the most recent spell's spend, so a later cheap spell turns off the +4 [M].
detail: last_spell_energy_spent is overwritten on every spell play (game_engine.cpp:1907). After a 4+ spell, playing a 1-cost spell drops the condition, although the text says 'if you've spent [4] or more to play a spell this turn'. A per-turn max or flag is needed.

name: Revna the Lorekeeper
summary: When the trigger snapshot is 0, it falls back to last_spell_energy_spent, which can belong to a different spell.
detail: For a 0-energy spell, the triggering_spell_energy_spent snapshot is 0. The fallback then reads the player's last spell spend and can wrongly ready Revna.

name: Smite
summary: The 'If it would die this turn, banish it instead' replacement only applies to the immediate 3 damage, not for the rest of the turn.
detail: Code banishes only when the 3 damage is lethal right away. If the unit survives and dies later this turn (combat, another spell), it goes to trash instead of being banished. The comment documents this.

name: Right of Conquest
summary: Always draws exactly 2 instead of 1 plus 1 per battlefield you control.
detail: Text says 'Draw 1, then draw 1 for each battlefield you or allies control.' Code calls drawCards(1) twice unconditionally and never counts controlled battlefields.

name: Scorchclaw
summary: Hunt 2 and Level 3 are wrong: XP is only gained at 3+ XP, Scorchclaw readies on conquer/hold, and +1 [M] / 'enter ready' are missing.
detail: Text: Hunt 2 = gain 2 XP on every conquer/hold. Level 3 = +1 [M] and enter ready while you have 3+ XP. The code's onTrigger returns if xp < 3 (so Hunt never fires below level 3), then adds 2 XP and readies the unit. There is no might aura and no entersReadyOnPlay. requiresLevel()/levelThreshold() are not consumed anywhere in the engine.

name: Square Up
summary: The [Repeat] cost 'Discard 1' is charged as part of every resolution, and the Repeat itself can never be paid.
detail: discardThenAct makes the player discard a card before Assault 4 is granted, even on the base cast. GameEngine::parseRepeatCost expects a '[' after '[Repeat]' and returns invalid for '[Repeat] — Discard 1', so the optional repeat is never offered.

name: Yeti Brawler
summary: 'if you assigned 3 or more excess damage' is treated as always true.
detail: Every conquer creates two Gold tokens regardless of excess damage (documented approximation). The def also sets Keyword::Reaction, which the card does not have. That keyword is mostly inert for units but is read by the Mystic Vortex reaction tax.

name: Dancing Grenade
summary: The 'Its controller may play this spell again for [A]' recast loop is not implemented.
detail: The comment documents that the recast hook is not wired. Only the escalating damage counter exists. That counter lives in card_counters and is never reset at end of turn, so a cast on a later turn also gets the bonus damage.

name: Grim Apothecary
summary: The unit to return is auto-picked (first friendly unit at any battlefield), and Apothecary itself is excluded.
detail: Text: 'you may return a friendly unit at a battlefield to its owner's hand'. The player cannot choose which unit; find_friendly_at_bf takes the first in map order. The text does not exclude Apothecary itself, but the code skips ctx.source.

name: Undying Legion
summary: '[Legion] You may play me from your trash for [3][R]' is not implemented.
detail: The class only returns requiresLegion()=true, which the engine never reads, and nothing grants a trash-play permission for this card. The card is a vanilla 3/3.

name: Red Brambleback
summary: 'Your conquer effects for conquering here trigger an additional time' is not implemented.
detail: The card documents this as an ENGINE GAP. Only the conquer buff is implemented.

name: Double Trouble
summary: Automatically takes the first unit among the top 3 (the 'may' is forced, with no player choice) and moves it to hand without a draw.
detail: Text: 'You may reveal a unit from among them and draw it.' Code always picks the first unit found, with no choice and no decline. It moves the card by editing zones directly, so no draw event fires. Recycle order is also not chosen.

name: Frisky Hunter
summary: Frisky Hunter itself has [Deflect] (deflect_value=1 + Keyword::Deflect), but only the Bird token should.
detail: The text gives Deflect only to the 1 [M] Bird token. The def sets d.deflect_value = 1 and Keyword::Deflect on the 3 [M] unit, so opponents must pay [A] to target it. The Bird token is also created by name rather than bound to card 559.

name: Herald of Spring
summary: [Hunt] (gain 1 XP when I conquer or hold) is not implemented.
detail: The only trigger is WhenYouPlayMe (+2 XP). Hunt is not handled generically by the engine; other Hunt cards such as Voracious Gromp implement it with WhenIConquerOrHold. Herald therefore never gains XP from conquer or hold.

name: Skyward Strike
summary: At Level 6 the stun replaces the move instead of being added to it, and the move always goes to base.
detail: Text: 'Move an enemy unit. [Level 6][>] [Stun] an enemy unit.' The Level 6 line is an additional effect that can target a different enemy unit. Code does either moveToBase or stunUnitBy on the same single target, so at 6+ XP the unit is never moved. The move destination is also fixed to base.

name: Back Off
summary: Draws 1 unconditionally, ignoring the 'If you played this from your hand' condition.
detail: The card has [Hidden], so it is often played from a facedown position, not from hand. Code always calls drawCards(1) and never checks the play source, for example current_play_source as Drag Under does.

name: Flurry of Feathers
summary: The counter mode pops the spell without calling revertCounteredPlay, which other counters such as Hard Bargain and Abandon call (CR 425.1.b).
detail: Mode 0 calls chain.items.pop_back() and disposeCounteredCard but skips revertCounteredPlay. Counter behaviour is therefore inconsistent with the other counter spells.

name: Forgotten Signpost
summary: Additional cost 'exhaust a unit you control' is paid at resolution rather than on activation.
detail: Exhausting the friendly unit is a cost. The code exhausts it inside onActivate, so the unit stays ready while the ability is on the chain and the cost is skipped if the ability fizzles or the unit was already exhausted in response.

name: Mosstomper
summary: Deflect is set unconditionally in def() (keywords + deflect_value=1), so Mosstomper always has Deflect and has Deflect 2 at Level 3.
detail: Text grants [Deflect] only at [Level 3]. def() sets Keyword::Deflect and deflect_value=1 permanently; deflectCostFor sums deflect_value plus each Deflect aura, so at 3+ XP opponents pay 2 instead of 1, and below 3 XP they pay 1 instead of 0.

name: Trevor Snoozebottom
summary: def() sets Keyword::Temporary on Trevor himself, so GameEngine::beginningStep kills him at his controller's next Beginning Phase.
detail: Only the Sprite token should have [Temporary]; Trevor's text just mentions the keyword. beginningStep kills every on-board object whose base keywords include Temporary, so Trevor dies one turn after being played.

name: Honeyfruit
summary: Level 6 ability adds 2 universal power instead of 1 Energy + 1 [A] power.
detail: [Add] [1][A] is one Energy plus one any-domain power (Platewyrm Egg uses addFloatingEnergy for [1]). Code calls addFloatingUniversalPower(ctx.controller, 2).

name: Honeyfruit
summary: Level 6 ability is offered and pays its [E] cost below 6 XP, then does nothing.
detail: Text says to use the ability only while you have 6+ XP. The XP gate sits inside onActivate after the exhaust has been paid, and neither activatedAbilities nor a canActivate override hides ability 1, so an agent can exhaust Honeyfruit for no effect.

name: Iascylla
summary: The delayed next-Main-Phase pull is abandoned if Iascylla leaves the board before it fires, and the pulled battlefield is stored on Iascylla's card_counters.
detail: The delayed trigger is independent of the source once created; the code returns early when ctx.source no longer exists (and the BF stash lives on the dead object). The candidate set also only includes enemy units already at a battlefield (excludes units at base, includes units already at this battlefield).

name: Ivern, Nurturer
summary: The revealed unit is the first unit found in the top 3 and the buffed friendly unit is the first unit in map order; neither is a player choice.
detail: Text lets the player choose which unit to reveal/draw (matters for the Bird/Cat/Dog/Poro rider) and which friendly unit to [Buff]. Code takes the first unit in deck order and the first friendly on-board unit in GameState::objects order (possibly one that already has a buff, wasting it). The drawn card is also moved to hand directly without a draw event.

name: Nami, Headstrong
summary: The 'next unit you play' ready+buff lets the agent pick any exhausted friendly unit rather than the unit that was actually played.
detail: Text affects exactly the next unit played this turn. Code arms on hold, then on any WhenYouPlayAUnit offers every exhausted friendly unit on board; it also does nothing if Nami has left the board after holding (the effect should persist).

name: Scuttle Crab
summary: 'You can look at their facedown cards this turn' is not implemented.
detail: Deathknell reveals the opponent's hand and gains 1 XP but grants no visibility of the opponent's facedown (Hidden) cards; XP is added directly without updating xp_gained_this_turn.

name: Tricksy Tentacles
summary: Moves a single enemy unit with Might 8 or less to base, instead of any number of same-controller enemy units with total Might 8 or less to one chosen location.
detail: Code has TargetRequirements count=1, max_might=8 and calls moveToBase. Multiple units cannot be chosen, the total-Might budget is not enforced across units, and battlefield destinations are never offered.

name: Yuumi, Magical Cat
summary: Yuumi gives only +3 Might; the [Tank] grant is missing and the target is not restricted to 'other units here'.
detail: Text: give one of your other units here +3 [M] and [Tank] this turn. Code calls giveTemporaryMight only (no giveTemporaryKeyword Tank), and TargetRequirements allow any friendly unit at any battlefield, including Yuumi herself.

name: Alpha Wildclaw
summary: 'Your units here with less Might than me can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities' is not implemented (documented engine gap).
detail: Only [Tank] is present; the protection clause is left as a comment explaining the engine cannot express it.

name: Lillia, Protector of Dreams
summary: def() gives Lillia herself [Tank] and the 'When you play a token unit, +1 [M] this turn' trigger is unimplemented.
detail: Text grants Tank only to your token units; Keyword::Tank is set in Lillia's own base keywords, forcing her to be assigned damage first. The first sentence (token-play trigger) is documented as an engine gap and missing.

name: Master Yi, Unstoppable
summary: Level cost reductions omit the [G] power portion and the Level 16 untargetability is unimplemented.
detail: Text reduces [2][G]/[4][G][G]/[6][G][G][G]; code reduces only 2/4/6 energy, so the card still costs 3 power at any level. [Level 16] 'can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities' is left as a documented engine gap.

name: Eclipse
summary: The [Predict] clause is never executed. Only the -4 [M] is applied.
detail: onResolve only calls giveTemporaryMight(-4). Keyword::Predict is set on the def, but no code in src/engine acts on that keyword (grep finds no engine use), so no predict happens. Compare Abandon, which implements its Predict inline.

name: Ruined Rex
summary: Deathknell damage hits the first enemy unit in map order at a battlefield instead of a player-chosen enemy unit.
detail: Text: deal 4 to an enemy unit (chosen, any location incl. base). Code iterates GameState::objects and damages the first enemy unit at a battlefield; no choice, units at base excluded, Deflect/untargetable ignored.

name: Turn to Dust
summary: Grants [Temporary] through giveTemporaryKeyword, which is revoked at the end-of-turn Expiration Step, so the gear is never killed.
detail: giveTemporaryKeyword sets temp_keywords, and expireTemporaryKeywords clears it at end of turn. The Beginning Phase kill sweep (game_engine.cpp beginningStep) always runs after that, so the effect does nothing. The grant should be permanent (obj.keywords.set), as in Fading Memories (0180).

name: Chakram Dancer
summary: def() gives Chakram Dancer herself permanent [Shield] (shield_value=1).
detail: Text only grants Shield to your other units here this turn; the card itself has no Shield. def() sets Keyword::Shield and shield_value=1, so she gets +1 Might whenever defending.

name: Crescent Strike
summary: Missing 'and 1 to each other enemy unit there'. The target is also not restricted to units at a battlefield.
detail: Code deals 4 to one enemy unit only. The splash damage to the other enemy units at that battlefield is absent. TargetRequirements lacks must_be_at_battlefield, so enemy units in base are legal targets.

name: Deadly Flourish
summary: The target is any unit instead of an enemy unit, and the 'when it dies this turn' watch never expires.
detail: TargetRequirements has no must_be_enemy, so friendly units are legal. The DelayedAbility has no expires_on_turn, so if the unit dies on a later turn the Gold token is still created.

name: Frigid Jewel
summary: The friendly unit that gets +2 [M] is picked deterministically instead of chosen by the player.
detail: Text says 'give a friendly unit +2 [M]'. Code gives it to the first friendly unit in the objects map, which is outcome-relevant (it may pick a unit at base).

name: Gustwalker
summary: Keyword::Ganking is set unconditionally in def(), so Gustwalker always has Ganking regardless of Level 3.
detail: Text grants [Ganking] only while you have 3+ XP; the base keyword makes the level gate meaningless for movement (the aura only adds the +1 Might correctly).

name: Petal Pixie
summary: def() sets Keyword::Temporary on Petal Pixie itself, so it is killed at its controller's next Beginning Phase and counts itself for its own bonus.
detail: The text only references units with [Temporary]; Pixie has no Temporary. beginningStep kills objects with base Temporary, and applyPassiveAura counts the Pixie itself, giving at least +1 Might.

name: Hwei, Brooding Painter
summary: Gear branch readies the first two exhausted runes in map order instead of letting the player choose.
detail: Text: ready up to 2 runes (player's choice); code picks automatically. Domains of runes can matter for power payment.

name: Lillia, Fae Fawn
summary: Sprite token is created at Lillia's destination instead of the location she moved from, enters ready, and Lillia herself has [Temporary].
detail: Text: when I move from a location, play the Sprite there (the origin). Code uses self.location (already the destination) although onUnitMoved stores __moved_from_bf; token is created with enter_ready=true though text doesn't say ready; def() sets Keyword::Temporary on Lillia so she dies at the next Beginning Phase.

name: Sprite Queen
summary: def() sets Keyword::Temporary on Sprite Queen herself, so she is killed at her controller's next Beginning Phase.
detail: Only the Sprite tokens should have [Temporary]. With the base keyword, beginningStep kills the Queen before (or around) her own AtStartOfBeginning token trigger.

name: Zilean, Time Mage
summary: The optional 'you may play an additional copy' is applied automatically.
detail: Text is a 'may' replacement; code always doubles the first friendly token unit each turn while Zilean is at a battlefield.

name: Blue Sentinel
summary: 'Hold effects here trigger an additional time' is unimplemented, and the [A] is added immediately on hold instead of at the start of the next Main Phase, where it is lost.
detail: Hold scoring happens in the Beginning Phase and rune pools empty at end of the draw phase, so the immediately added [A] is wiped before the controller can use it. Nothing in TriggerManager::onScore doubles hold triggers at this battlefield.

name: LeBlanc, Everywhere at Once
summary: LeBlanc is given [Temporary] herself, and her static suppresses all triggers of Temporary units instead of stopping the Temporary kill.
detail: Printed LeBlanc has no Temporary, but def() sets Keyword::Temporary, so beginningStep kills her. Per rules the [Temporary] keyword is itself the triggered 'kill me' ability; the intent is that your Temporary units at her battlefield are not killed. Instead TriggerManager::fireTrigger skips every trigger of a Temporary unit there, and beginningStep's kill loop is never suppressed.

name: Dragonsoul Sage
summary: Keyword::Reaction is set on the unit card although [Reaction] applies only to its activated ability.
detail: Unit plays don't use the Reaction keyword for timing, but extraAnyPowerCost treats Reaction-keyword cards as subject to reaction taxes (Mystic Vortex), so playing Sage could be taxed incorrectly.

name: Call to Battle
summary: The destination battlefield and the opponent's unit are chosen by heuristics, not by the players.
detail: The caster's destination is the first controlled battlefield. The opponent's unit to move is auto-picked as their highest-Might unit; the text gives that choice to the opponent. Both choices can change the outcome.

name: Crowd Favorite
summary: Spend 2 XP is paid at resolution, not as an activation cost.
detail: ActivationCost is empty and XP is deducted in onActivate; the ability can be activated (and use the chain) without the cost being paid up front.

name: Disposal Order
summary: Which of the up to 3 trash cards to recycle is not chosen. It always takes the 3 most recent, and never fewer.
detail: Text: 'Choose up to 3 cards from opponents' trashes.' Code takes the last 3 in the trash with no player choice.

name: Gentle Gemdragon
summary: Readies runes on ANY friendly unit play instead of only when you play another Dragon, and probably fires twice on its own play.
detail: Text: when you play me or another Dragon. Code subscribes to WhenYouPlayAUnit with no Dragon tag check (documented approximation), so every unit play readies up to 2 runes; if WhenYouPlayAUnit also fires for Gemdragon's own play, it readies 4. Runes readied are the first exhausted ones in map order, not chosen.

name: Imposing Challenger
summary: Destination 'a different battlefield' is the first other battlefield, not a player choice.
detail: Only matters when 3+ battlefields exist (token battlefields).

name: Stare Down
summary: Gains 1 XP when pickTarget suspends and again on re-entry, so a normal resolution gives 2 XP. The battlefield is also chosen heuristically.
detail: pickTarget always publishes a prompt and returns kInvalidId at resume_point 7. The kInvalidId branch then adds 1 XP and returns, and the resumed pass adds another 1. The battlefield is auto-picked as the one with the most eligible enemies instead of being a player choice.

name: Wily Newtfish
summary: PlayerState::xp_gained_this_turn is never incremented anywhere, so Wily Newtfish never gets +1 Might or Ganking.
detail: grep shows xp_gained_this_turn is only declared, reset in resetTurnTracking, and read here; all XP gains in cards are raw `ps.xp += n` with no tracker update. The condition is permanently false.

name: Blood Rose
summary: 'Ready a unit' is restricted to friendly units.
detail: Text says 'Spend 3 XP, [E]: Ready a unit.' (any unit). The ability's TargetRequirements set must_be_friendly = true, so enemy units can never be chosen.

name: Clash of Giants
summary: Damage is attributed to the spell (ctx.source) rather than to the units that deal it.
detail: Text: 'They deal damage equal to their Mights to each other.' Marching Orders passes the units as sources, but this card passes ctx.source, so 'when this unit deals damage' style triggers would not see the units as sources.

name: Irresistible Faefolk
summary: The moved enemy unit is the first enemy in map order, not a player choice; untargetable/Deflect is ignored.
detail: Text: you may move an enemy unit (chosen) to that battlefield. Code only asks yes/no then moves find_enemy_elsewhere()'s first hit.

name: Master Yi, Tempered
summary: Deflect (deflect_value=1) and Ganking are set unconditionally in def(), so the Level 6 gate is ignored.
detail: Text grants [Deflect] and [Ganking] only at 6+ XP. Base keywords give them always; at 6+ XP the extra Deflect aura makes the deflect cost 2.

name: Arachnoid Horror
summary: Both 'can be played to an occupied battlefield if an enemy unit is alone there' clauses are unimplemented.
detail: The class only implements [Hunt 2]; no play-location hook exists in the card or engine (no grep hits for 'alone' in game_engine.cpp).

name: Elder Dragon
summary: 'Choose up to one enemy unit at each location' always picks the first enemy at each location.
detail: No player choice of which enemy (or none) per location; with the any-damage-lethal aura this choice decides which unit dies.

name: Crescent Guardian
summary: The [P] optional cost is offered even if no spell was played this turn (then wasted), and 'played a spell' is detected via last_spell_energy_spent > 0, missing 0-cost spells.
detail: Text makes the additional cost available only if you've played a spell this turn. Code always offers it; the ready is gated on last_spell_energy_spent > 0, so a played 0-energy spell does not count and paying without a spell burns the [P] for nothing.

name: Isolate
summary: The 'enemy unit alone at that battlefield' check counts only enemy units and ignores the caster's units there.
detail: Code draws if exactly one enemy unit remains, even when friendly units share the battlefield. Under a reading of 'alone' as the only unit there, it would draw incorrectly.

name: Megatusk
summary: Megatusk has Keyword::Ganking permanently in def(); text only grants Ganking via the Spend 3 XP ability this turn.
detail: The base keyword makes Megatusk always able to move battlefield-to-battlefield. Also the 3 XP is spent at resolution rather than as an activation cost (ActivationCost is empty).

name: Blast Cone
summary: 'When you move an enemy unit, you may exhaust this to stun it' only works right after its own play trigger.
detail: The second sentence is a separate standing trigger that should fire whenever you move an enemy unit (with spells, abilities, and so on). The code only offers the stun inside the WhenYouPlayThis handler, and no move-event trigger exists for later moves.

name: Blast Cone
summary: The 'may move an enemy unit' effect always moves it to its base and picks the first enemy if no target is pre-supplied.
detail: Move could also go to a battlefield. Code calls moveToBase, and find_enemy() picks the first enemy unit by map order instead of asking the player.

name: Scryer's Bloom
summary: Predict 2 keeps the unrecycled cards in reversed order with no ordering choice.
detail: Text says to put the rest back in any order. Kept cards are pushed back in peek order, which reverses the original top-two order, and the player gets no reordering decision.

name: The List
summary: The named tag is chosen by a heuristic (most common enemy tag), not by the player.
detail: 'As you play this, name a tag' is a player choice. onPlay picks the most frequent tag among enemy units on board, and names nothing if the opponent has no units, which disables the card permanently.

name: Bone Skewer
summary: The caster's 'You may choose a unit' is forced: a hand unit must be picked whenever one exists.
detail: This is documented in the code as a GAP. pickTargetPair offers no decline option for the second pick.

name: Conscription
summary: The 5 XP is deducted again on every re-entry after pickTarget suspends, so the player pays 10 XP and can go negative.
detail: confirmOptional returns the stored 'yes' on re-entry. onResolve re-runs from the top after pickTarget suspends, so 'ps.xp -= 5' runs twice with no affordability recheck. The additional cost is also paid at resolution instead of at play. The 'recall' is done with moveToBase, which emits UnitMovedEvent, although a recall is not a move (CR 457-458).

name: Heedless Resurrection
summary: The additional cost 'kill a friendly unit' is paid at resolution, not at play.
detail: If the spell is countered, no unit is killed. The kill also happens inside the effect. This is documented as an engine limitation. The revived unit always enters at base.

name: Maduli the Gatekeeper
summary: 'I can't be readied' is not implemented (documented engine gap).
detail: Maduli readies normally in the Awaken step and from effects, which is a major drawback missing from a 7-cost 6 Might unit.

name: Baron Nashor
summary: "Other friendly units have +2 [M]" is not implemented anywhere.
detail: The class has no applyPassiveAura override and no engine code references Baron's anthem; only the Pit creation and untargetability are implemented. Every other friendly unit should get +2 Might while Baron is on the board.

name: Vex, Apathetic
summary: "They can't move it this turn" is not implemented (TODO in code).
detail: Only the stun is applied; the played unit can still be moved by its controller this turn.

name: Carrion Dredger
summary: Carrion Dredger itself is given [Deflect] although only its Bird token should have it.
detail: def() sets deflect_value=1 and Keyword::Deflect on the Dredger; the Deflect in the text (and its reminder) refers to the Bird token. Opponents wrongly pay [A] extra to target the Dredger.

name: Loyal Poro
summary: "Didn't die alone" only counts friendly units still on the board, so units that died simultaneously (e.g. in the same combat) don't count.
detail: CR intent is 'other friendly units were here' at the moment of death; the check runs at trigger resolution and scans only objects whose current location equals Poro's last_location, missing co-deaths.

name: Ultrasoft Poro
summary: Ultrasoft Poro itself is given [Deflect]; only the Bird tokens should have it.
detail: Official text has no Deflect keyword for the Poro (the reminder text refers to the tokens), but def() sets deflect_value=1 and Keyword::Deflect.

name: Ultrasoft Poro
summary: "Use only while I'm at a battlefield" is checked against any copy the controller has, not the activating object.
detail: canActivateAbility returns true if any Ultrasoft Poro the player controls is at a battlefield, so a second copy at base can activate. Should use the per-object canActivateAbilityAt variant.

name: Mageseeker Investigator
summary: Multi-unit move surcharge is inert (code comment admits it).
detail: applyPassiveAura sets BattlefieldState::surcharge_enemy_multi_move but nothing charges [A] per additional unit when an opponent moves several units to this battlefield; the card is effectively vanilla.

name: Safety Inspector
summary: Opponent's forced kill is auto-picked (lowest Might) instead of the opponent choosing; XP additional cost is offered at trigger resolution, not as a play cost.
detail: Text says each player kills one of their units (their choice); code kills the opponent's lowest-Might unit. The optional 3-XP additional cost is asked inside the trigger rather than during play, which can change outcomes (e.g. XP state after responses).

name: Shadow's Call
summary: [Temporary] is granted through giveTemporaryKeyword and expires at end of turn, so the unit is never killed. The 'without [Temporary]' filter is also missing.
detail: The temp keyword is revoked in the Expiration Step before the controller's next Beginning Phase, so Draw 2 comes with no drawback. enumerateLegalTargets does not exclude units that already have [Temporary].

name: Stalking Wolf
summary: Mandatory sacrifice is a post-play trigger, not an additional cost, and the 'play me to its battlefield' clause is unimplemented.
detail: Wolf can be played with no Bird/Cat/Dog/Poro to kill (then nothing is sacrificed), and cannot be Ambushed to the sacrificed unit's battlefield without other units there. Both deviations are documented in the code comment.

name: Undying Loyalty
summary: The Power cost gate ('no more than [A]') is ignored, and the [2] discount applies when any tagged unit is in trash rather than when one is chosen.
detail: eligible() checks only energy_cost <= 2, so units with a Power cost of 2 or more are legal. selfCostReduction gives the discount whenever a Bird/Cat/Dog/Poro unit of any cost is in trash, even if it is not an eligible target or is not chosen.

name: Ashe, Focused
summary: "When they hold, return it to their hand" is not implemented; the banished card is lost forever.
detail: The log text says the hold-return rider is not implemented; no delayed ability is registered, which makes the card a permanent discard instead of a temporary one.

name: Atakhan
summary: Optional 'kill a friendly unit to reduce my cost' additional cost is unimplemented; defender's kill is auto-picked.
detail: Atakhan always costs full 10/3 (the code comment calls it an engine gap). The attack trigger kills the defender's lowest-Might unit here instead of letting the defender choose (simplification).

name: LeBlanc, Fragmented
summary: 'Your Beginning Phase' check ignores whose turn it is and misses the Scoring Step.
detail: Code draws 2 whenever phase == BeginningStep, including the opponent's Beginning Phase; per CR 315.2 the Beginning Phase also includes the Scoring Step (where hold-related deaths occur), which draws only 1.

name: Sacrifice
summary: The additional cost 'kill a friendly Mighty unit' is paid at resolution. If no Mighty unit remains then, nothing is drawn or channeled.
detail: The cost should be paid when the spell is played. Here, if the Mighty unit is removed or shrunk in response, the spell resolves with no effect. If the spell is countered, no unit is killed.

name: Shard of Undoing
summary: The opponent's 'kill one of their units' choice is made by a lowest-Might heuristic.
detail: Each opponent chooses which of their units to kill. Code always kills the opponent's lowest-Might unit with no agent decision.

name: Vi, Peacekeeper
summary: Attack trigger never stuns: triggered abilities receive empty targets, and onTrigger returns when targets is empty.
detail: TriggerManager passes empty targets to triggers (see trigger_manager.cpp:372 comment) and chooseTargetsAtFinalize only fills targets for spells/activated abilities, so Vi's stun is dead code. Also enumerateLegalTargets is not limited to 'here' (any battlefield).

name: Poppy, Defender of the Meek
summary: Optional 'spend 3 XP to cost [3] less' is forced whenever the player has 3+ XP, and the XP is deducted later in a trigger.
detail: The 'you may' is not offered; the player always pays 3 XP when able. The XP deduction happens at WhenYouPlayMe resolution, so it can be skipped if XP dropped in between while the discount was already applied.

name: Rift Herald
summary: Move trigger always draws the first unit found instead of letting the player choose (or decline).
detail: 'You may reveal a unit from among them' is forced and the choice of which unit is the first in deck order.

name: Rift Herald
summary: Deathknell plays the unit totally free; its Power cost is not paid.
detail: Text: ignore Energy cost but still pay Power cost. Code calls playIgnoringCost, so Power is ignored too (comment admits approximation).

name: Curtain Call
summary: [Repeat] never works: the engine's parseRepeatCost can't parse '[Repeat] — [1] / [A] / [1][A]', so the spell can't be repeated.
detail: GameEngine::parseRepeatCost skips whitespace after '[Repeat]' and needs '['. It finds the em dash and returns invalid, so no Repeat tranche is ever offered. The header also says it supports only one cost, while the three tranches cost [1], [A] and [1][A]. Curtain Call always resolves exactly one mode.

name: Curtain Call
summary: All modes share one optional play-time unit target, so a repeated Curtain Call can't deal 2 to one unit and give -4 to another, and modes 1/3 vs 2 depend on where that single target is.
detail: Each repeat should make its own choices (CR 820.2). Here a single targets[0] is chosen at play and reused by every mode. Also used_mask lives in card_counters on the spell object and is never cleared, so if the same card object is cast again later, modes used earlier stay blocked.

name: Pridestalker
summary: 'Give a unit +1 [M]' target is chosen heuristically (the played unit, else first friendly unit at a BF) rather than by the player.
detail: Text lets the controller pick any unit; the code never asks (no pickTarget) and in the fallback restricts to friendly units at battlefields, ignoring base units.

name: Thrill of the Hunt
summary: Battlefield choice is never offered: pickMode after pickTarget always returns 0, so the unit is always played to the first battlefield.
detail: pickTarget leaves resume_point at 8 (finalize path and resolve path both); pickMode then sees resume_point>=5 and returns resume_data[1], which pickTarget/finalize padded with 0. The 'any battlefield' choice collapses to battlefields[0] with no prompt. Card helpers only compose in pickMode-then-pickTarget order (Resonating Strike notes this).

name: Thrill of the Hunt
summary: Banished tokens come back, and the replayed unit keeps damage/buffs/stun/empowered state.
detail: banishObject leaves a token object alive in zone Banishment (it just skips the banishment list), and the card then calls playIgnoringCost on it, so a token returns instead of ceasing to exist (CR 183.1). Unlike Temporal Breach (853), which returns early for tokens and resets damage_marked/buff_count/temp_might_bonus/is_stunned/empowered, Thrill resets nothing, so the 'new object' carries over its old state.

name: Lilting Lullaby
summary: 'Counter a spell' always targets the top chain item; if the top is an ability (or another spell is wanted) the card does nothing.
detail: hasLegalTargets accepts any spell anywhere in the chain, but onResolve only looks at chain.items.back() and returns silently if it is not a spell, so the lockout is also skipped. The player can't pick which spell to counter.

name: Green Father
summary: Replaces the first controlled non-Brush battlefield instead of 'that battlefield' (the one just conquered/held).
detail: find_target() iterates state.battlefields and returns the first one the controller controls; it ignores the trigger's subject (the scored battlefield card, available via triggering_subject / triggeringBattlefield helper). When the player controls both battlefields, the wrong one can be replaced.

name: Daisy!
summary: Stun target is the first unstunned enemy unit in map order rather than a player choice.
detail: 'Stun an enemy unit here' should let the controller choose; code picks the first matching object.

name: Moonfall
summary: Both the battlefield and the enemy unit to move are picked by heuristic (first in map order), not by the player.
detail: chooseBattlefield returns the first battlefield where the controller has a unit, and find_movable_enemy returns the first enemy unit not already there. The player only answers yes/no. Which battlefield gets the -2 and which enemy is pulled in changes the outcome.

name: Deceiver
summary: Optional 'discard 1 and exhaust me' cost is chosen and paid at resolution, not at finalization.
detail: No choicesAtFinalization() opt-in, unlike sibling legends (Green Father, Gloomist); per CR 383.3 the may/cost is decided when the trigger is finalized.

name: Void Assault
summary: Both units are forced to the same destination; the text moves each unit independently. The 'you're the attacker' rider is also not applied (documented ENGINE GAP).
detail: One pickMode destination is applied to both targets[0] and targets[1]. The rules allow the friendly and enemy units to go to different legal destinations. The attacker designation when both land at a battlefield you don't control is missing.

name: Keeper of the Hammer
summary: 'When you hold, gain 1 XP' uses WhenIConquerOrHold, so XP is also gained on every conquer.
detail: onScore fires WhenIConquerOrHold for both score methods; the card should use TriggerType::WhenIHold. Doubles the XP rate for aggressive decks.

name: Keeper's Verdict
summary: Top/bottom is chosen by the spell's controller; the text says the unit's owner chooses.
detail: pickMode publishes the choice to ctx.controller ('Its owner places it on the top or bottom'), so the caster picks top or bottom for the opponent's unit. Also a token sent this way is put into the deck instead of ceasing to exist (CR 183.1).

name: Amateur Recital
summary: Hold trigger is a no-op: it relies on targets[0], which triggered abilities never receive.
detail: This is the same engine path as Navori: a triggered ability's chain item has empty targets, so moveToBase is never called. The 'you may' is also unmodeled (it would be forced if targets did arrive). It needs confirmOptional + pickTarget over units at any battlefield.

name: Star Spring
summary: The player says yes/no, but the engine moves the first unit in the list instead of letting the player choose which unit goes to base.
detail: The text says 'they may move another unit they control here to its base', which is the player's choice of unit. The code moves movable[0] (map order) after confirmOptional, with no pickTarget and no choicesAtFinalization. The played unit is also found with a 'newest id' heuristic, because the trigger carries no subject.

name: Valley of Idols
summary: The played unit is found by a newest-non-token-id heuristic, so playing a token unit here is never handled.
detail: The trigger carries no subject. Tokens don't emit CardPlayedEvent (createToken emits only EnteredBoardEvent), and the heuristic excludes tokens anyway, so 'plays a unit here' misses token units.

name: Vaults of Helia
summary: The +1 cost modifier has no unit filter, so it also taxes the holder's non-token spells and gear this turn.
detail: The text says 'your non-token units cost [1] more'. The CostModifier sets only energy_increase and affects_non_token_only. In GameEngine's cost loop (game_engine.cpp ~5653) the only type filters are next_spell_only, next_unit_only and gear_only, so every non-token card the player plays this turn costs +1. CostModifier has no persistent units-only flag.

name: Lonely Poro
summary: 'Died alone' ignores friendly units that died at the same time, so a simultaneous combat wipe counts as dying alone.
detail: The check runs at trigger resolution and only scans objects still at the death location; co-dying friendly units are already in the trash, so Lonely Poro draws even though it was not alone when it died.

name: Piltover Enforcer
summary: 'Ready a unit' target set restricted to friendly units.
detail: Text says 'ready a unit' (any unit); findTargets only includes units controlled by the legend's controller. Rarely matters but narrows legal choices.

name: Wuju Master
summary: [Level 11] 'Your units enter ready' is not implemented.
detail: applyPassiveAura only grants the Level 6 +1 [M]; the Level 11 tier is a comment-only 'ENGINE GAP'. An analogous enter-ready hook now exists in GameEngine::resolvePermanent (The Exile, id 956), so it is implementable. (The stale comment claiming legend auras don't run is also outdated: recalculateAuras now includes LegendZone objects.)

name: Scorn of the Moon
summary: 'Spend this Energy only during showdowns' restriction is not enforced; adds unrestricted floating Energy.
detail: onActivate calls addFloatingEnergy (general pool) and the trace admits the earmark is not engine-enforced; the energy can be spent on main-phase plays.

name: Astral Heron
summary: 'First card each turn' is checked as cards_played_this_turn == 1 at resolution, so a card played in response cancels the discount.
detail: If the controller plays another card (e.g. a Reaction) before the trigger resolves, the counter is 2 and no cost modifier is created, though the trigger condition was met when it fired.

name: Renekton, Brute
summary: "When my Might becomes 10 or more, empower me" is not implemented, so his Empowered Deflect/Ganking never turns on by itself.
detail: Only the [1]: +1 [M] ability and the Empowered aura exist. Nothing checks current_might >= 10, no trigger is declared, and nothing in src/engine references this card. Renekton only becomes Empowered through other cards (Profiteer, Tornado Warrior).

name: Spiderling
summary: "I have +1 [M] for each other unit you control here with my name" is not implemented.
detail: The class has no applyPassiveAura; only Hidden (keyword) and unlimited_copies are set, and no engine code references Spiderling. A stack of Spiderlings at one battlefield stays at 1 Might each. The only test (Vendetta_Spiderling_AnyNumberOfCopies) checks deck construction only.

name: Twilight Step
summary: needsPlayTimeTarget() makes the engine ask for a target at finalization (and charge Deflect), but onResolve ignores it and asks for the unit again.
detail: chooseTargetsAtFinalize prompts and stores ri.targets (paying Deflect for that unit). onResolve at resume_point 0 builds its own objChoice prompt from scratch, so the agent picks twice. The moved unit can differ from the one chosen (and paid Deflect for), and the resolve-time pick charges no Deflect.

name: Shuriken Flip
summary: The hand-built enemy prompt bypasses Deflect: a Deflect enemy can be damaged without paying [A].
detail: The enemy choice uses objChoice/takenObject, not pickTarget, so affordableWithDeflect/commitChoice never run. The chosen enemy's Deflect cost is not checked or paid.

name: Curator of the Sands
summary: 'Ready up to 2 runes' readies the first two exhausted runes in map order instead of letting the player choose which (domain matters).
detail: No pickTarget; readies runes[0..1] from object-map iteration order, so the domain of readied runes is arbitrary. Also the optional exhaust cost is paid at resolution with no choicesAtFinalization opt-in.

name: Shadow Dash
summary: Same as Twilight Step: the target chosen at finalization is ignored and re-prompted at resolution.
detail: needsPlayTimeTarget() is true, so the engine chooses an enemy target at finalization (with Deflect). onResolve then issues a fresh objChoice prompt over dashTargets and moves whatever was picked there. Deflect is not charged for that pick, and the player is asked twice.

name: Defender of Tomorrow
summary: Gear to ready is picked automatically (first exhausted friendly gear) rather than chosen.
detail: 'Ready a gear' / 'Ready 2 gear' readies the first N exhausted friendly gear in map order with no agent choice.

name: Kinkou Temple
summary: Checks only u.keywords (printed/temporary Tank), so units with aura-granted Tank don't get +1 [M].
detail: Uses keywords.has(Tank) instead of hasKeyword. The in-code comment acknowledges the gap.

name: Risen Altar
summary: The '[1] or [A] less' discount is always applied as [1] Energy; the [A] alternative is not modeled.
detail: The discount is also keyed to the battlefield's controller rather than the owner of each unit here.

name: Riven, Broken Blade
summary: The WhenIBecomeExhausted hook fires on any exhaustObject call, including on a unit that is already exhausted, so Riven/Reckless Innovator can trigger without 'becoming' exhausted.
detail: EffectExecutor::exhaustObject sets is_exhausted=true and always emits ObjectStateChangedEvent 'exhausted'. TriggerManager::onObjectStateChanged (trigger_manager.cpp:1126) fires WhenIBecomeExhausted without checking the previous state. An effect that exhausts an already-exhausted Riven therefore gives a free mode, and a free Gold or draw for Reckless Innovator. The fix is to skip the emit when obj.is_exhausted was already true.

name: Riven, Broken Blade
summary: The heal/exhaust/recall death-replacement paths set is_exhausted without emitting 'exhausted', so 'When I become exhausted' misses them.
detail: The self-replacement recall (game_engine.cpp ~6313), the Altar of Blood recall (~6364) and effect_executor.cpp ~193 set unit.is_exhausted=true directly and emit only 'healed'. A ready Riven or Reckless Innovator that is recalled this way becomes exhausted but does not trigger. This is an edge case.

name: Riven, Broken Blade
summary: In the stun mode, the buff is still spent when the chosen enemy is no longer legal at resolution (mistarget), so the buff is lost for nothing.
detail: Case 1 decrements buff_count first and only stuns if tgt is still valid. When pickTarget returns kInvalidId at resolution (mistarget), the buff is spent with no stun. Whether 'spend my buff to X' should be skipped entirely when X has no legal target is a rules question, so confidence is low. Separately, the card_counters writes before finalizingChoices (lines 24-26, 38) are internal bookkeeping and are idempotent across the two passes, so they are not a problem.

name: Blade of the Exile
summary: Equip attaches for free when neither [A] nor a ready friendly unit is available.
detail: If there is no synergy unit, payableOnePower is false, and `other` is kInvalidId, pay_unit stays kInvalidId. The `return false` check only triggers when the gear itself doesn't exist, so execution falls through to attachFree without any cost being paid.

name: Blade of the Exile
summary: The choice between paying [A] and exhausting a unit is a hardcoded heuristic (card ids 957/961), not a player decision.
detail: The player should choose which equip cost to pay and which unit to exhaust. Code prefers specific card ids, then [A], then the first ready unit. It also excludes the unit being equipped from the units that can be exhausted, though text allows any friendly unit.

name: Bedeviling Stranger
summary: "you may return an enemy unit" is forced: pickTarget has no decline option, so the bounce always happens when a candidate exists.
detail: onTrigger goes straight to pickTarget, which publishes one MakeChoice per legal target and no 'none' option (card.cpp pickTarget). There is no confirmOptional. A 4+-unit battlefield therefore always bounces an enemy unit. This matters when the controller would rather keep, for example, a stunned or damaged enemy on the board. The 'choose a battlefield' step is folded into the target pick (acceptable).

name: Hunker Down
summary: 'It can't move this turn' is not implemented.
detail: onResolve readies the unit and draws 1. The comment admits the can't-move restriction is not modeled (no engine flag), so the readied unit can move or attack the same turn.

name: Ki Burst
summary: Official text stuns 'a unit' (any unit) but the target requirement is must_be_enemy.
detail: TargetRequirements{.must_be_enemy = true} rules out stunning your own unit (e.g. to protect it, or for stun-matters synergies). The official text has no friendly/enemy restriction.

name: Ki Burst
summary: The additional cost (exhaust a friendly unit) is paid at resolution, and an engine heuristic picks the unit (prefers card ids 957/961).
detail: The cost should be paid when playing and chosen by the player. Here it is skipped if the spell is countered, and the stun fizzles if no ready friendly unit remains at resolution. The unit to exhaust is picked by hard-coded preference, not by the agent.

name: Hunters' Circle
summary: The card's only effect (first unit/gear played here on your turn costs [1] less) is not implemented.
detail: The class only supplies def(), and a NOTE comment says the discount is not modeled. The battlefield has no effect at all.

name: Battle Preparations
summary: Show Off is checked at resolution (not at play/finalization), and the runes to ready are picked automatically.
detail: CR 832.1.c.2: the decision to Show Off is made while finalizing the spell. The code checks at resolution for any gear in hand or on board, so a gear that left in between changes the result. 'Ready up to 2 runes' readies the first two exhausted runes in map order with no player choice of which runes (domain matters).

name: Rakelstake
summary: Only unit plays trigger it; gear played here never triggers the Predict.
detail: The text says 'play a unit or gear here'. The class listens only to WhenYouPlayAUnit, on the assumption that gear is always played at base, which misses effects that play gear to a battlefield.
